title: DBEFNet: a dual-branch fusion network integrating remote sensing imagery and building morphology for urban village segmentation
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Urban villages (UVs) are informal settlements embedded within Chinese cities, and their boundary delineation is fundamental to urban renewal and refined spatial management. However, accurate segmentation of UVs relies on both visual characteristics and the spatial organization of buildings, yet previous studies have often relied on simplified representations of building morphology that inadequately capture spatial configuration. We propose DBEFNet, a dual-branch encoding and fusion framework that exploits remote sensing imagery (RSI) and building morphology heatmaps for fine-grained UVs segmentation. The RSI branch combines CNN and Swin Transformer encoders with multi-scale feature extraction to capture and integrate local appearance and broader spatial context. In the Building branch, multiple building attributes are transformed into morphology heatmaps and adaptively weighted to characterize building-cluster patterns. A hybrid attention fusion module (HAFM) models bidirectional dependencies between visual semantics and building morphology. Experiments across 15 cities yielded an overall accuracy (OA) of 94.79 % and a mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 86.24 %. Ablation experiments indicate that incorporating building morphology improves mIoU by 0.87 % over the enhanced RSI-only model, while adding the HAFM provides further gains of 0.93 %. Compared with the RSI-only model, DBEFNet achieved higher mIoU in 11 of the 15 cities, with an average city-wise gain of 1.92 %. Trained on Beijing, DBEFNet achieved 75.79 % mean mIoU across 12 unseen target cities, demonstrating its cross-city generalization capability. These results underscore the critical role of building morphology and the value of integrating morphological cues with visual appearance for precise UVs mapping.

title: Application of Mobile-DOAS observations for analyzing sub-pixel variability and comparing TROPOMI-derived NO x emissions over the Yeosu-Gwangyang industrial complex
abstract: This study investigates sub-pixel spatial variability in TROPOMI NO2 observations and its impact on the consistency between TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS observations for the Yeosu-Gwangyang industrial complex in South Korea. Furthermore, NOx emissions are estimated using both datasets and compared with a bottom-up emission inventory. The comparison of co-located TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS observations shows good correlation (r = 0.86), with TROPOMI data exhibiting a slight underestimation relative to the Mobile-DOAS observations (-8.5%). The underestimation was more pronounced when Mobile-DOAS observations had limited spatial coverage within the satellite pixel and was reduced when the spatial coverage increased, indicating the importance of spatial representativeness of ground-based measurements. The analysis of TROPOMI NO2 columns with the Exponentially Modified Gaussian (EMG) emission analysis reveals a decreasing trend in NOx emissions from 2021 to 2025 (-29%), along with pronounced seasonal variability. In comparison, Mobile-DOAS-derived emissions show substantial variability across individual measurement rounds and no clear seasonal pattern. A comparison of TROPOMI and Mobile-DOAS emission estimates with bottom-up emission inventory data indicates reasonable comparability, although differences vary across the observation periods. The weekend-to-weekday emission ratios range from 0.80 to 0.90, indicating a weak weekend effect consistent with the industrial characteristics of the region. Overall, this study highlights that (1) sub-pixel variability affects the consistency between satellite and ground-based observations and should be explicitly accounted for in satellite validation studies, and (2) satellite, Mobile-DOAS, and bottom-up estimates provide complementary information for quantifying NOx emissions over industrial regions.

title: Coarse-to-fine physics-guided reconstruction of gridded sea level anomalies from HY-2B/C/D altimetry
abstract: The capability of the Chinese HY-2B/C/D altimeter constellation for gridded sea level anomaly (SLA) reconstruction using only HY-2 observations remains insufficiently evaluated. This study presents a physics-guided framework designed for near-real-time (NRT) SLA reconstruction in the Northwest Pacific and retrospectively evaluates it using 2022−2025 HY-2B/C/D observations. The framework combines an OI-derived coarse background with deep-learning refinement, with target-period reconstruction driven solely by HY-2B/C/D along-track data. Validation against an identical set of 1255 independent tide-gauge observations yields mean RMSE of 0.051 m and a mean correlation coefficient (r) of 0.83 over 12 tide-gauge stations. Inter-product comparisons during 2022−2025 show closer agreement with the DUACS DT and NRT products than with NSOAS, although differences in SLA reference conventions and geophysical correction standards among the products should be considered when interpreting regional discrepancies. Scale-dependent evaluation using SARAL/AltiKa along-track observations indicates a mean effective spatial resolution of approximately 300 km. Dynamical consistency is further assessed against surface-drifter observations using geostrophic velocity anomaly magnitude, yielding mean RMSE of 0.181 m s−1 and r of 0.54. These results demonstrate that spatially coherent and dynamically plausible daily SLA fields can be reconstructed with HY-2B/C/D as the sole altimetric observations during the target period, supporting the potential of the proposed framework for NRT SLA reconstruction under sparse observational constraints.

title: Gravity-conditioned diffusion for seafloor bathymetric resolution enhancement
abstract: Global bathymetric products such as SRTM15+ provide extensive ocean coverage but cannot resolve many fine-scale seafloor features captured by shipborne multibeam surveys. Generative reconstruction methods can reconstruct more detailed terrain, but they may also introduce plausible-looking structures that are not supported by observations. We propose GravBathy-Diff, a conditional diffusion framework that uses observed low-resolution bathymetry as its primary input and incorporates satellite-altimetry-derived marine gravity as an auxiliary physical constraint. The gravity-differential enhancement module jointly encodes bathymetry, terrain derivatives, and the co-registered gravity field at the input stage. Gravity-conditioned time–frequency modulation regulates the contribution of gravity across diffusion stages and feature bands, while gravity-guided attention focuses this information on the spatial locations and feature channels where it is most useful. Deflections of the vertical, gravity anomalies, and vertical gravity gradients derived from Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) wide-swath altimetry are compared as alternative conditioning fields. Experiments are conducted on real SRTM15+ –multibeam bathymetry pairs from four ocean regions and assessed using depth error, perceptual similarity, terrain derivatives, and spectral fidelity. GravBathy-Diff achieves the strongest overall performance among the evaluated regression, adversarial, and diffusion methods, with the exception of one regional gradient-RMSE result. It ranks first on all six metrics averaged over four additional ocean areas and remains effective on an independent public digital elevation model (DEM) benchmark at 4×. Among the three gravity representations, the vertical gravity gradient provides the most effective guidance for reconstructing local relief. These results show that marine gravity can support the recovery of fine-scale seafloor structure while reducing high-frequency artifacts that are inconsistent with the available observations.

End-to-End Differentiable Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics for Fluid--Rigid Optimization with Gradient Stabilization
abstract: We introduce an end-to-end differentiable optimization framework for Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) with fluid–rigid body coupling. The central difficulty is not only to obtain local derivatives of SPH operators, but also to propagate useful sensitivities through long rollouts whose particle neighborhoods, contacts, and pressure responses change rapidly over time. These effects make reverse-mode gradients noisy and often cause adjoint variables to explode in long-horizon control and inverse-design tasks. We formulate an SPH-specific reverse-mode pipeline for IISPH-based fluid–rigid simulation and implement the required vector–Jacobian products within checkpointed simulation segments. To make the resulting gradients usable for optimization, we introduce a self-adaptive adjoint correction sequence that acts as a descent-preserving preconditioner: it bounds pathological adjoint amplification while keeping the update direction aligned with the original reverse-mode sensitivity. Our experiments cover a sequence of increasingly demanding tasks, from low-dimensional impulse and shape optimization to scalar-amplitude water actuation, multi-object water-jet balancing, and neural fluid-mediated pendulum control. These results demonstrate that stabilized reverse-mode differentiation can support challenging SPH-based optimization problems involving indirect momentum transfer, long-horizon event timing, and high-dimensional control.

title: Consistency-Aware Map Generation at Multiple Zoom Levels Using Aerial Image
abstract: The multi-level tiled map service is widely used and serves as a kind of digital infrastructure. These map tiles are usually rendered from vector data, whose update needs to walk or drive with professional equipment to check every points of interest. This leads to inconvenience and expensive cost in timely updating maps. Compared with vector data, aerial images are much easier and cheaper to obtain. In this paper, we propose a novel multi-level map generation framework that can automatically generate accurate and consistent maps with multiple zoom levels from aerial images. It consists of a level-aware map generator and a consistency-aware map generator. The level-aware map generator is able to generate accurate initial maps with realistic details for each zoom level. The consistency-aware map generator regards initial maps at each zoom level as a sequence and builds the connection between them, so as to guarantee content consistency between maps at different zoom levels. Furthermore, we collect a large-scale high-quality dataset called Multi-Level Map (MLM) for map generation at multiple zoom levels. Experiments on our MLM dataset show that our method outperforms previous state-of-the-art map generation methods on both comprehensive quantitative metrics and perceptual quality.

title: Over-the-Air Semantic Alignment via Dual Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces
abstract: Semantic communications enable task-oriented information exchange, but suffer from latent-space mismatch when transmitter and receiver employ heterogeneous machine learning models. Existing semantic alignment methods rely on digital processing, introducing computational and latency overhead. This paper proposes a dual stacked intelligent metasurfaces (dual-SIM) architecture that performs semantic alignment entirely in the wave domain. By jointly exploiting programmable metasurfaces at both ends of a link and the wireless channel, the proposed architecture realizes an end-to-end linear transformation between heterogeneous latent spaces. We show phase-only multilayer SIM can approximate both supervised linear aligners and zero-shot Parseval-frame equalizers. We investigate single-SIM, disjoint asymmetric and symmetric dual-SIM, and jointly optimized dual-SIM configurations, considering channel equalization and constructive channel exploitation. For joint design, we develop an alternating projected gradient algorithm with convergence guarantees to first-order stationary points. We further introduce a deep-unrolled network that unrolls gradient-based iterations to reduce computational cost of SIM reconfiguration under channel variations. Numerical results with heterogeneous vision transformer encoders show accurate semantic alignment from moderate to high signal-to-noise ratios. The joint and symmetric disjoint dual-SIM designs achieve the highest accuracy over compact channels, the joint design leads at shallow stack depths, and the advantage over single-SIM designs diminishes at equal depth.

title: PALIN: Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR Multimodal 3D Object Detection with Benchmark
abstract: 3D object detection is critical for intelligent transportation systems. LiDAR has been widely adopted for accurate geometric measurements; however, purely geometric representations remain ambiguous under sparse observations and occlusions, while cross-sensor multimodal fusion suffers from calibration and synchronization errors. To overcome these challenges, we leverage an Ouster LiDAR to construct PALIN (Pixel-Aligned LiDAR-NIR), a large-scale intrinsically pixel-aligned multimodal dataset jointly capturing geometry and NIR intensity, comprising approximately 8,000 annotated frames from static urban intersections and diverse mobile suburban scenes. Building upon this dataset, we propose CMambaFusion, a novel fusion framework consisting of a four-directional Cross-Mamba module for bidirectional cross-modal interaction and a Gated Concat-Mamba module for joint feature refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PALIN enables effective multimodal learning, and CMambaFusion achieves superior accuracy-efficiency trade-offs over both LiDAR-only and representative fusion baselines.

title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
abstract: Hyperspectral models of fish freshness rarely transfer between species, and labelling a new species is slow and destructive. Freshness is also ordinal, and standard domain alignment can erase that order. We present InvarOrd, which adapts to a new species from 30 labelled cubes (5 per rank) in three stages: self-supervised spectral pretraining on unlabelled source cubes, cross-species alignment by a shrinkage covariance discrepancy computed only within matched ranks, and ordinal distillation into a compact student. The alignment term is provably invariant to the rank means, so it gives no incentive to collapse the ordinal axis. On paired salmon and cod data (800 cubes each, 16 days), a source-trained teacher reaches 1.6 to 1.9 days mean absolute error (MAE) on the other species, with quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) below zero. The 423K-parameter student, 2.54 times smaller than its teacher, attains the lowest MAE (1.476 days) and highest within 1-day accuracy (56.1%) among 14 configurations, matching the best of six ImageNet-pretrained backbones (ConvNeXt-T, 1.503 days) at 66 times fewer parameters, 1.44ms per cube on a GPU and 5s re-adaptation. InvarOrd beats target-only training by 0.29 days (p = 0.031). Among alignment objectives, rank-invariant alignment retains the most ordinal structure (embedding rank correlation 0.183, QWK 0.112), whereas global discrepancy lowers the rank correlation to 0.049 and QWK to zero at only 0.014 days higher MAE.

title: Detecting Small Space Objects for Space Situational Awareness with Collaborative Edge AI
abstract: With the rapid growth of space activities, near-Earth space is becoming increasingly congested, leading to a higher risk of spacecraft collisions and space debris generation. Recent close-proximity encounters and collision incidents necessitate efficient and cost-effective onboard systems for space object detection (SOD) and collision avoidance. While deep learning (DL) enabled Edge AI using low-cost vision sensors on single or multiple satellites has shown promises for SOD, significant challenges remain, including limited datasets, small SOD, and the lack of comprehensive performance assessments. This paper presents a collaborative Edge AI framework for multiview SOD and systematically benchmarks DL models and fusion strategies. Results show that higher image resolution significantly improves small SOD. For multiple views, image-level fusion reduces the combined communication and inference latency by 30.13% and 32.80% on average compared with feature-level and attention-based fusion across the evaluated inter-satellite link (ISL) bandwidth. For larger view sets, feature-level and attention-based fusion achieve better detection accuracy at the cost of analysis in the sensing-communication pipeline, revealing that multiview collaboration introduces minimal latency overhead under ISL constraints when reception capacity is not exceeded. Our work provides valuable design insights for future collaborative satellite network design, supporting the emerging space situational awareness and space traffic management requirements.

title: XLSAR-Bench: Towards Extremely Large SAR Imagery Understanding of MLLMs
abstract: The rapid development of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) has highlighted the need for comprehensive benchmarks to assess their capabilities and limitations in remote sensing (RS). However, evaluating MLLMs in large-size synthetic aperture radar (SAR) scenarios remains challenging, as understanding complete scenes requires both global semantic interpretation and fine-grained target perception. Existing SAR benchmarks predominantly rely on small image patches, limiting their ability to assess these capabilities jointly. To address these limitations, we present XLSAR-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark for evaluating the perception and reasoning capabilities of MLLMs in large-scene SAR imagery. XLSAR-Bench comprises 405 images with an average size of 7153$\times$7153 pixels, ten tasks spanning visual question answering, visual grounding, and detailed image captioning, with all evaluation samples meticulously annotated manually, assisted by a semi-automatic captioner. Experimental results from general-purpose and domain-specific MLLMs reveal persistent challenges in understanding large SAR scenes and accurately perceiving small targets. We have open-sourced XLSAR-Bench to support further research in developing more powerful MLLMs for complete large SAR scenes.

title: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
abstract: SAR-to-optical translators often synthesize detail that the radar measurement does not support, and pixel metrics alone cannot reveal it. We propose SAR-TopoGuard, a training-free inference-time layer for frozen generators: a stochastic sampler draws K candidates (Monte Carlo dropout for GANs, seed variance for diffusion), a speckle-aware verifier ranks them by gradient-magnitude correlation with the SAR input and a hallucination-frequency index, and a SAR-guided frequency gate admits high-frequency detail only where SAR edges support it. With all five hyperparameters frozen and three training seeds, we evaluate on 500 scene-disjoint SEN1-2 test patches, 500 patches of a held-out summer scene, and 200 cross-dataset SEN12MS winter pairs. The layer improves Pix2Pix by +0.060, +0.012, and +0.077 dB PSNR and by +0.0034, +0.0057, and +0.0135 SSIM, respectively (Wilcoxon p < 1e-6), and it improves CycleGAN and CUT on all three sets (+0.013 to +0.076 dB). It raises edge precision at the cost of edge recall (edge F1 -1.3% on the test set). On the latent diffusion model COP-GEN, it adds +0.33 dB (base) and +0.16 dB (Beta) on the winter set, the only set with dual-polarization SAR. An ablation shows that the gate produces the gain for MC-dropout GANs, whose candidates are nearly identical, whereas verifier selection contributes up to +0.26 dB for diffusion, whose samples differ. The layer has zero trainable parameters and adds 0.4 ms per patch beyond the K=5 generator passes.

title: Attribution-Guided Shared-Private Decoupling for Noise-Reduced Audio-Visual Representation Learning
abstract: Audio-visual representation learning commonly aligns paired audio and visual signals with sample-level contrastive objectives. However, real-world audio-visual pairs usually contain heterogeneous patch tokens: only a subset carries reliable cross-modal shared semantics, while many others mainly encode modality-private residuals. Aggregating all tokens into a single global representation can therefore introduce semantic noise into cross-modal alignment. Motivated by the minimal-sufficiency principle, we propose an attribution-guided shared-private decoupling framework to mitigate this issue. Our key idea is to identify shared-cover subviews that preserve dominant cross-modal information while suppressing modality-private residuals, and use them to supervise decoupled shared and private representations. To identify such subviews efficiently, we draw on transformer attribution method and introduce Layer-Truncated Attribution (LTA), which provides a lightweight estimate of token-level relevance to cross-modal shared information. We further adopt a teacher-student framework, where the teacher provides attribution-induced supervision and the student internalizes shared-private decoupling into its representations, without introducing extra inference cost. Experiments on retrieval, classification, and sound-prompted semantic segmentation show consistent gains over strong baselines. Compared with baseline, our method improves the average zero-shot R@1 by 4.0 across AudioSet and VGGSound retrieval, and improves AS20K classification mAP by 3.1, demonstrating the effectiveness of fine grained attribution guidance for reducing semantic noise.reducing semantic noise. Code will be released at https://github.com/wanglg20/LTA

title: Puzzle: One Pass Is Not Enough for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation
abstract: Open-vocabulary remote sensing image segmentation (OVRSIS) enables the segmentation of unseen classes without additional annotation or retraining. By analyzing the predictions of existing OVRSIS methods, we find that many misclassified patches coexist with visually similar, correctly classified patches of the same class within the same image. Unfortunately, most of these methods stop after a single inference rather than using their predictions to guide further inference. Motivated by this observation, we propose \textbf{Puzzle}, a plug-and-play iterative re-inference framework that combines prediction history with a visual-similarity prior to progressively refine patch-level attention. Puzzle employs a lightweight history-conditioned controller to regulate each patch's contribution as an information source and its reliance on visually similar patches, while an adaptive stopping rule determines when to stop. It keeps the segmentation model frozen and reuses the same controller across different models and datasets without retraining. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent performance improvements across diverse OVRSIS models and datasets, highlighting the strong transferability of Puzzle. Moreover, Puzzle can further improve the performance of SOTA methods.

title: FDAM: A Frequency-Direction-Aware Multi-Task Framework for Pavement Crack Grid Localization
abstract: Pavement crack grid localization remains challenging for thin and tiny cracks due to weak visual cues and background interference. Box detection often misses these cracks, while supervised semantic segmentation faces limited pixel-wise annotations and high labeling costs. In this paper, we propose a Frequency-Direction-Aware Multi-Task framework (FDAM) with box detection and grid classification branches. The core grid classification branch comprises Frequency-Domain Enhancement (FDE) and Directional Feature Refinement (DFR). FDE adaptively weights spectral bands and fuses reconstructed features with spatial features. DFR captures thin crack patterns through multi-scale strip convolutions, direction-sensitive modulation, and feature recalibration. Sparse positive cells and ambiguous local predictions motivate adaptive grid supervision. Adaptive Importance Reweighting emphasizes uncertain predictions and local label transitions, with focal supervision for all cells. Our contribution is to couple the box detection and grid classification branches through shared feature learning for pavement crack grid localization. We validate FDAM on our RoadDistress2026 dataset of thin and tiny cracks and further evaluate it on public datasets Crack500 and DeepCrack. The code is available at https://github.com/Lab-PANbin/FDAM

title: Beyond the Training Cameras: Coverage-Controlled Probes of Viewing Direction in Frozen Vision Models
abstract: Vision models are trained on 2D images of a 3D world. Do their hidden features encode the direction from which the camera views a scene, and if so, in what form? We study the relative viewing direction $α$ of two objects in rendered scenes where both object centres stay at fixed pixels while the camera moves, so that perspective, shading and shadows change but the projected layout does not. In eight pretrained models, from diffusion models to self-supervised and image-text encoders, $α$ is encoded in a strikingly simple form: a single two-dimensional plane in the hidden space, shared across scenes, in which the difference between the two objects' features traces $(\cosα, \sinα)$. The plane keeps its orientation when lighting, colours, floors and object shapes change. This encoding is more than a summary of a few visible measurements: readouts fitted on one set of camera paths stay accurate at camera positions outside their range in seven of the eight models, whereas decoders of the measured object and shadow geometry, equally accurate within that range, fail there. In the diffusion transformer PixArt-$α$, the plane forms abruptly at a single block and carries direction information to later blocks, yet editing it changes the objects rather than the generated viewpoint. We also examine how this encoding carries over to scanned real objects.

title: Hyperspectral remote sensing of cover crop traits for decision support in precision nitrogen management
abstract: Spaceborne hyperspectral sensors offer opportunities to quantify crop traits and inform variable rate nitrogen management, yet their operational use remains limited. We evaluated PRISMA and EMIT imagery across four winter cover crop seasons in Maryland, U.S., to predict traits required by the open source Cover Crop Nitrogen Calculator (CC-NCALC) decision support tool. Traits included aboveground biomass, nitrogen concentration (N%), non-structural carbohydrates (NSC%), holocellulose (HCL%), and lignin (LIG%). Using these traits as inputs, the CC-NCALC estimates nitrogen credits from cover crops based on decomposition dynamics informed by trait data, soil, and weather conditions. Nitrogen credits are the estimated amount of plant available nitrogen that a cover crop contributes to the subsequently planted cash crop. Trait models were developed using partial least squares regression with several cross validation strategies. Biomass ( R 2 = 0.70–0.87; RMSE = 661–951 kg ha −1 ), NSC% ( R 2 = 0.69–0.72; RMSE = 4.53–7.63%), and HCL% ( R 2 = 0.65–0.70; RMSE = 5.04–7.50%) predictions were strong. But HCL% and NSC% predictions degraded under cross-scene and cross-species validation ( R 2 = 0.47–0.54; RMSE = 6.06–9.18%). N% ( R 2 = 0.15–0.79; RMSE = 0.46–0.74%) and LIG% ( R 2 = 0.02–0.35; RMSE = 1.22–1.83%) predictions were more variable; predictions using EMIT were more accurate than predictions using PRISMA, but both approaches demonstrated the need for further increases in accuracies of retrieval approaches for these two traits. Spring trait maps from April 2024 were ingested into the CC-NCALC to estimate nitrogen credits, which ranged from −14.58 to 45.65 kg N ha −1 , with higher values associated with greater legume biomass. Inter-scene comparisons demonstrate EMIT's increased spectral fidelity and trait prediction accuracy compared to PRISMA. Results demonstrate that integrating spaceborne hyperspectral imagery with decision support systems can generate site-specific nitrogen credit maps, advancing hyperspectral remote sensing toward operational nutrient management. Future missions will be critical to help scale these approaches for routine on-farm use.

title: Spatiotemporal variability in seasonal and interannual InSAR-derived excess ground ice content retrievals using Sentinel-1
abstract: The melting of excess ground ice in ice-rich permafrost regions causes elevated ground subsidence through soil thaw consolidation at landscape scales. The increased subsidence due to melting of excess ice is unaccounted for in current InSAR-based retrievals of season thaw depth, or active layer thickness (ALT); this omission may lead to overapproximated ALT estimates compared to in situ. We processed Sentinel-1 interferometric data spanning 2018–2023 over the Drew Point and Teshekpuk Lake region. Using a novel degree-day of thaw regression on InSAR displacement time series, we estimated total seasonal subsidence and found elevated subsidence during warmer years which we attribute to the melting of excess ice. Integrating these seasonal subsidence estimates into the remotely sensed active layer thickness (ReSALT) algorithm yielded consistently overapproximated ALT estimates. In conjunction with independent estimates of ALT, we exploited this positive bias in ReSALT to estimate excess ice within the active layer. We found agreement between InSAR estimates of excess ice and in situ measurements within uncertainty for warmer years. We observed a positive spatial correlation between seasonal subsidence and excess ice in the active layer with proximity to surface hydrological features. Furthermore, we observed that InSAR-derived subsidence decreases with older drained lakes, and InSAR-derived excess ice decreases with increasingly degraded ice wedge polygon type. We discovered that thaw season intensity has a first order effect on the temporal variability of seasonal subsidence and excess ice content, and the success of our method is contingent upon warm thaw seasons.

title: High resolution sediment-specific surface soil moisture retrieval using Sentinel-1 time series and auxiliary data
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: In this study, we examine the potential of continuous ground moisture monitoring over a mining site using a combination of in-situ soil moisture sensors and multi-sensor SAR images. We focus on assessing and improving methodologies for retrieval of surface soil moisture, i.e. ground moisture, from SAR measurements focusing on detailed in situ reference observations for several key geomaterials, i.e. sediments, typical in the study site. The mining site represents a limestone quarry located in the southeastern Finland. Our hypothesis is that sediment-specific well-calibrated models can be instrumental in improving soil moisture retrieval under different weather conditions to produce spatially explicit soil moisture estimates at high resolution compared to baseline approaches. Studied SAR data are represented by Copernicus Sentinel-1 C-band images, while auxiliary datasets include optical Sentinel-2 data. Reference data were collected using IoT enabled capacitance sensors. The reference data were calibrated based on laboratory analyses conducted on the different sediment types studied, including organic soil, clay, gravel, and flotation sand. The examined machine learning (ML) methods include XGBoost, LightGBM, random forest, support vector regression, linear regression and k-nearest neighbors. The performance of ML algorithms was evaluated using different cross-validation techniques including a five-fold approach as well as Leave-One-Sensor-Out (LOSO) to assess predictive accuracy and transferability to unseen sensors. The best performance under random five-fold cross-validation was achieved with the most comprehensive feature set which combines Sentinel-1 backscatter, time-series based soil moisture indices (SMI), Sentinel-2 optical, topographic, and temperature predictors. SHAP analysis revealed that SAR based features such as VH backscatter, traditional SMI derived from VV backscatter, and incidence angle were among the most important multi-source predictors. Adding sediment information improved Sentinel-1-only retrievals by more than 2 vol-%, but provided little additional benefit when richer multi-source feature sets were used. In the best sediment-area-level configurations, RMSE decreased to 0.037–0.050 m 3 m − 3 (3.7-5.0 vol. % points ), with R 2 values reaching 0.90. Accuracy varied by sediment texture, with the lowest errors for clay and organic soil and higher errors for flotation sand and gravel. However, LOSO validation demonstrated substantially weaker and site-dependent transferability: R 2 ranged from 0.45 to 0.67 for organic soil at a southern site and from 0.07 to 0.21 for organic soil at a northern site. Thus, high within-dataset predictive accuracy did not translate uniformly to unseen sensor locations, highlighting the need for broader spatially independent validation.

title: Process-informed deep learning for interpretable forested wetland mapping under dense canopy
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Canopy-obscured hydrologic signals and gradual wetland–upland transitions hinder the delineation of forested wetlands, particularly when heterogeneous Earth-observation evidence is fused as an unstructured feature stack. We developed a process-informed multi-stream convolutional neural network (CNN) for mapping forested wetlands on a 10-m modelling grid in the Changbai Mountains, China. The model used 85 covariates derived from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, ALOS-2 PALSAR-2, and Copernicus DEM GLO-30. These covariates were assigned a priori to five predictor streams and processed by separate CNN branches before fusion. Relative to a capacity-matched single-stream baseline, the grouped architecture increased forested-wetland F1 by 3.42 percentage points across five validation folds, whereas the gain on the fixed held-out test set was smaller (+1.03 percentage points). For map production, the probability-averaged five-fold ensemble achieved an overall accuracy of 0.873, a macro-F1 of 0.882, and a forested-wetland F1 of 0.836 on the fixed held-out test set. To interpret correlated predictors, group-aggregated SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and k-nearest-neighbor conditional replacement were used to characterize global and conditional model reliance. Among correctly classified forested-wetland samples, global reliance was greatest for temporal features and phenology, whereas conditional replacement indicated the greatest residual model reliance for hydrology, followed by topography. Direct pixel counting yielded a map-derived forested-wetland area of 686.6 km 2 , concentrated mainly in peripheral plains and hills. This framework combines process-informed feature organization with dependence-aware interpretation to support interpretable regional mapping of canopy-obscured forested wetlands.

title: Generative Point Cloud Registration With Match-ControlNet
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel 3D registration paradigm, Generative Point Cloud Registration, which bridges advanced 2D generative models with 3D matching tasks to enhance registration performance. Our key idea is to generate cross-view consistent image pairs that are well-aligned with the source and target point clouds, enabling geometry-color feature fusion to facilitate robust matching. To ensure high-quality matching, the generated image pair should feature both 2D-3D geometric consistency and cross-view texture consistency. To this end, we introduce DepthMatch-ControlNet and LiDARMatch-ControlNet, two matching-specific, controllable 2D generative models. Specifically, for depth camera-based 3D registration with point clouds derived from the depth maps, DepthMatch-ControlNet leverages the depth-conditioned generation capabilities of ControlNet to synthesize perspective-view RGB images that are geometrically consistent with depth maps, ensuring accurate 2D-3D alignment. Additionally, by incorporating a coupled conditional denoising scheme and coupled prompt guidance, it further promotes cross-view feature interaction, guiding texture consistency generation. To address LiDAR-based 3D registration with point clouds captured by LiDAR sensors, LiDARMatch-ControlNet extends this framework by conditioning on paired equirectangular range maps projected from 360$^\circ$ LiDAR point clouds, generating corresponding panoramic RGB images. Our generative 3D registration paradigm is general and can be seamlessly integrated into a wide range of existing registration methods to improve their performance. Extensive experiments on the 3DMatch and ScanNet datasets (for depth-camera settings), as well as the Dur360BEV dataset (for LiDAR settings), demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach.

title: Image Quality Assessment for Machine-oriented Communication
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: The rapid development of Multimoal Large Language Models (MLLMs) has driven the evolution of communication paradigms, making the transmission of visual information in extremely low-bandwidth possible. However, as it is oriented toward computer vision tasks rather than humans, there is no widely accepted metric for its evaluation. To address this issue, we conduct a comprehensive visual quality assessment of machine oriented communication systems. Specifically, we (1) at the source level: a generative codec framework is established, with a MLLM communication pipeline through cross-modal generation between images and text. (2) at the channel level: images are transmitted using channel encoding/decoding strategies in different physical environments, and construct a dataset with 12k pairs of reference/distorted images. (3) at the sink level: 50 computer vision models are implemented to conduct 600k inferences on 5 downstream tasks, to characterize the differences between refer ence/distorted image pairs. (4) at the evaluation level: benchmark 18 cutting-edge Image Quality Assessment (IQA) methods, and develop a novel Mixture-of-Experts metric, termed CFA-MoE, to serve as a strong baseline for this task. Experimental results show that the current IQA algorithms cannot accurately evaluate machine-oriented distortions, highlighting the importance and challenge of this task. It is expected this dataset and baseline to facilitate future IQA algorithms and promote the communication paradigms from human to machine preference. Code will be available at: https://github.com/aiben-ch/MoQAD.

title: SpaRRTa: A Synthetic Benchmark for Evaluating Spatial Intelligence in Visual Foundation Models
abstract: Abstract Visual Foundation Models (VFMs), such as DINO and CLIP, excel in semantic understanding of images but exhibit limited spatial reasoning capabilities, which limits their applicability to embodied systems. As a result, recent work has incorporated some 3D tasks (such as depth estimation) into VFM training. However, VFM performance remains inconsistent across other spatial tasks, raising the question of whether these models truly possess spatial awareness or overfit to specific 3D objectives. To address this question, we introduce the Spatial Relation Recognition Task (SpaRRTa) benchmark, which evaluates the ability of VFMs to identify static directional relations between visible objects. Unlike traditional 3D objectives that focus on precise metric prediction (e.g., surface normal estimation), SpaRRTa probes a fundamental capability underpinning more advanced forms of human-like spatial understanding. SpaRRTa generates an arbitrary number of photorealistic images with diverse scenes and fully controllable object arrangements, along with freely accessible spatial annotations. Evaluating a range of state-of-the-art VFMs, we reveal significant disparities in their ability to encode directional spatial relations. Through our analysis, we provide insights into the mechanisms that support or hinder this form of spatial awareness in modern VFMs. We hope that SpaRRTa will serve as a useful tool for guiding the development of future spatially aware visual models. Our project page can be found at https://sparrta.gmum.net/ .

title: LEAD++: Unsupervised Fine-Grained Visual Representation Learning with Multi-context Enhanced Entropy-Based Adaptive Distillation
Block-Wise Variable Conditional Diffusion for High-Fidelity Text-to-4D Generation
abstract: Abstract Text-to-4D scene generation is currently impeded by three primary challenges: the prohibitive memory cost of training high-dimensional diffusion models, the semantic misalignment arising from the failure to disentangle static object identity from dynamic motion in text conditioning, and the scarcity of high-quality datasets that accurately correlate subjects, motions, and environments. To surmount these challenges, we present Swin4D , an end-to-end framework for efficient and high-fidelity text-to-4D synthesis. First, we introduce a Block-wise Variable Conditional Diffusion strategy, which mitigates memory constraints and prevents overfitting by dynamically reconfiguring spatial dependencies during training. Second, we propose Global–Local Alignment , a hierarchical guidance mechanism that explicitly disentangles global scene context from local subject-action semantics via separate T5 and CLIP encoders, ensuring spatiotemporal consistency and fine-grained semantic fidelity regardless of prompt length. Finally, we address data limitations by curating RealSynth4D , a large-scale hybrid dataset combining 108k real-world captures with 72k AI-synthesised scenes, establishing robust correlations between subjects, actions, and complex backgrounds to significantly enhance model generalisation.

title: Incremental Learning of Vision-Language Models via Task Subspace Projection and Dynamic LoRA
Editorial Board
RAVEN-Bench: A Paired EO-IR Video QA Benchmark for Aerial Multimodal Understanding
abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have advanced rapidly in image and video understanding, yet their ability to reason over paired aerial electro-optical and infrared (EO-IR) videos remains poorly understood. Such video poses a harder test than standard RGB video QA: targets are often small, evidence may appear only briefly, viewpoints change with the platform, and useful cues may appear in only one stream. We introduce RAVEN-Bench (Reasoning over Aerial Videos with EO-IR aligNment), a paired EO-IR video QA benchmark for low-altitude aerial multimodal understanding. RAVEN-Bench contains 100 temporally aligned EO-IR video pairs and 1,200 human-authored four-way multiple-choice questions, each independently audited for answer keys, modality requirements, evidence intervals, and group validity. It supports EO-only, IR-only, and paired EO+IR evaluation, and uses hierarchical capability levels and structured question groups to diagnose paired-input gain beyond the stronger unimodal condition, unimodal reliance, target consistency, and evidence-chain coherence. We evaluate frontier, open-weight, and remote-sensing MLLMs, showing that aggregate accuracy can overstate evidence-supported EO-IR reasoning. RAVEN-Bench provides controlled modality conditions and group-level diagnostics for auditing whether progress on RGB video benchmarks transfers to aerial cross-spectral understanding. Code and data are available at https://github.com/yuhu990424/RAVEN-Bench and https://huggingface.co/datasets/TerraSenseAnalytics/RAVEN-Bench.

title: Polynomial-Time Solvability of the Multi-Dimensional Slope Change Problem
abstract: Slope change detection seeks to identify changes in the trends of time-ordered signals. We study the problem of fitting a multidimensional time series by continuous piecewise-linear functions with a shared continuous breakpoint and unrestricted slopes. We consider both the dense setting, in which every dimension may change slope, and the sparse setting, in which at most $k$ dimensions may change slope. Although the resulting optimization problems are nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear programs and may have irrational optimal solutions even for rational data, we prove that all six variants, corresponding to the $\ell_1$, $\ell_2$, and $\ell_\infty$ losses in both settings, are exactly solvable in polynomial time. For least-squares loss, we obtain efficient algorithms requiring $O(JT)$ operations in the dense setting and $O(J^2T\log J)$ operations in the sparse setting, where $T$ is the number of time points and $J$ is the number of dimensions. We implement these least-squares algorithms and evaluate them on simulated data and three real-world time series, namely, surface temperatures (ERA5), hand-tracking data from a mixed-reality headset (HoloAssist), and turbofan engine sensor data (NASA C-MAPSS). The dense algorithm solves instances with up to $J=10^5$ and $T=100$, that is, $10^7$ observations, in less than $0.1$ seconds on a laptop, while the sparse algorithm solves instances with about $10^3$ dimensions and up to $T=240$ in under a second. Compared with a mixed-integer nonlinear programming (MINLP) formulation solved by Gurobi, our algorithms are several orders of magnitude faster (approximately $8.9 \times 10^3$ to $3.4 \times 10^6$ times) on instances where Gurobi terminates within its default optimality tolerance of $0.01\%$ optimality gap. On larger instances, Gurobi frequently reaches a 10,000-second time limit with substantial optimality gaps.

title: Box-conditional Hypothesis Testing for Out-of-Distribution Object Detection
abstract: Detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) objects is essential for ensuring the reliability and safety of object detectors in real-world deployment. We treat the decision on a detected box as a hypothesis test with the null hypothesis that the box covers an object of an in-distribution (ID) class. The null distribution changes with the size of the box and its contact with the image border, and the detector observes both. The test can therefore rank a box only against ID boxes of the same size and border contact, which gives a distribution-free bound on the false-alarm rate for each of them and uncovers the separation that one null distribution hides. The power of the test also rests on the layer it reads. Layers built only for the ID classes have no reason to keep what sets an unknown object apart, so the test reads the features before them. We propose \textbf{PLUM}, a training-free score that pools the last backbone stage inside the box and ranks its distance to the ID classes among ID boxes of the same size and border contact. On the standard benchmark, PLUM reaches the highest AUROC among the compared methods without external models, with 91.5 and 94.5 on PASCAL-VOC and 95.1 and 97.5 on BDD100K. Code: https://github.com/DDOZMI/PLUM

title: Enhanced Hyperspectral Nano-FTIR Imaging by Neural-Network-Based Processing of Multiple Signal Harmonics
abstract: Nano-FTIR spectroscopy combines infrared spectroscopy with nanometer-scale spatial resolution and enables hyperspectral nanoimaging. However, quantitative measurements typically rely on higher-harmonic near-field signals, which are largely background-free but suffer from low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). Lower harmonics provide substantially higher SNR but contain significant background contributions that distort the near-field response and hinder quantitative analysis. Here, we introduce a cross-harmonic neural network (CHNN) that exploits the complementary information encoded in multiple harmonic channels to denoise third-harmonic hyperspectral data. Trained directly on experimental nano-FTIR datasets, the CHNN uses first- and second-harmonic spectra to improve the SNR of the third-harmonic response. Applied to a PMMA/PS polymer blend, it substantially reduces noise while preserving spectral features and nanoscale spatial contrast. Compared with conventional single-harmonic denoising using an autoencoder, the CHNN achieves superior noise suppression. These results demonstrate the potential of lower-harmonic signals for improving hyperspectral nano-FTIR imaging without increasing acquisition time.

title: MaskSCD: Bitemporal Mask Classification for Semantic Change Detection in Remote Sensing Images
abstract: Semantic change detection (SCD) identifies where the land surface has changed and which land-cover transition has taken place. Most deep SCD networks predict the change map and the land-cover map of each date with separate per-pixel decoders. These outputs need not agree, so a pixel can be labeled as changed although it has the same class at both dates, and per-pixel decisions fragment objects. We present MaskSCD, which formulates SCD as the mask classification of a bitemporal label-pair image. Each bitemporal segment, a region of constant land-cover class pair, is predicted as one mask shared by both dates together with one class per date, and the change map is derived from the predicted class pair. This formulation keeps the change and semantic maps consistent and the label space linear in the number of classes. A bitemporal masked-attention transformer decoder implements it by reading each segment in both images and relating the two readings, and a bitemporal fusion pyramid provides per-date and change-aware features. MaskSCD is evaluated on SECOND, Landsat-SCD and Hi-UCD, which span 0.1 to 30 m resolution and four to nine land-cover classes, against fourteen recent SCD models re-trained under one protocol. MaskSCD achieves the best separated kappa, semantic change $F_1$ and transition $F_1$ on all three datasets and exceeds the strongest competitor by about five points in mean separated kappa. It produces no contradictory change pixels, which account for nearly 30% of the predicted change of some multi-task networks. The code is available at https://github.com/EricYu97/MaskSCD.

title: Unlocking Cross-Attention in Label-Scarce Regimes: A Weakly Supervised Approach for Video Semantic Segmentation
abstract: Weakly Supervised Video Semantic Segmentation (WS-VSS) aims to learn temporally consistent semantic object masks in videos using only video-level labels. While fully supervised models successfully learn temporal relationships by means of cross-attention, training these temporal weights under weak supervision is unstable and even pushes the model below its single-frame baseline. Therefore, existing WS-VSS methods exploit temporal consistency by relying on external priors, such as optical flow. Unfortunately these cues are non-semantic, computationally expensive and noisy, degrading the supervisory signal. Instead of supervising attention weights directly or using external priors, we propose MemCAM, a WS-VSS transformer framework that learns temporal cross-attention directly through feature-space self-supervision. MemCAM introduces a CAM Propagation Algorithm that synthesizes a supervisory signal by propagating past CAMs according to patch-level feature similarities in the latent space. Specifically, we constrain their induced CAMs through a consistency objective between predicted and propagated maps, stabilizing temporal attention learning. Experiments on the YouTube-Objects v2.2 and WS$^2$ datasets demonstrate that MemCAM consistently outperforms the temporal localization and segmentation performance of WS-VSS alternatives, showing that cross-attention can be effectively trained in label-scarce video settings through internal self-supervision.

title: Lens: Training-Free Semantic Search for Cross-Tile Object and Scene Retrieval in Satellite Imagery
abstract: We developed Lens, a training-free system for semantic object and scene search across large satellite mosaics that requires no detector trained for the class of interest. Lens represents each tile with a frozen, self-supervised vision transformer (DINOv3), removes the positional bias in its dense features by projecting them onto the subspace orthogonal to a positional basis estimated once from a constant image, and centers the debiased features on the mean feature computed across the whole area before comparison. Lens forms a query by averaging the centered features of a small neighborhood of patches around a chosen point, or of an entire tile for scene-level search, and matches it against the index by cosine similarity. It stores the centered patch features in a byte-quantized similarity index that supports real-time range search over a mosaic of thousands of patches, and a coarser whole-tile embedding index for scene-level retrieval. A guided upsampling network (AnyUp) runs once per tile to recover pixel-accurate boundaries beyond the native feature grid, and the result is cached so later queries reuse it. We evaluated Lens on the 5,128-tile DFC2020 test set and ran it as an interactive tool on five Sentinel-2 areas spanning agricultural, industrial, and desert terrain; the pipeline is not tied to a specific sensor. On DFC2020 a single click reaches 0.09 to 0.80 pixel F1 across eight land-cover classes at the per-class best threshold, with a mean F1 of 0.39, and it beats a pairwise INSID3 baseline on six of the eight classes at roughly four hundred times lower query cost. Indexing 1.31 million patches takes 169 s on one CPU thread, and a click returns a rendered overlay in 6 to 10 ms.

title: SWAM: Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging for Efficient Vision Transformers
abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) achieve strong performance on image recognition tasks, yet their quadratic self-attention complexity over input tokens creates prohibitive computational costs for practical deployment. Token reduction methods offer a practical solution by progressively reducing the token sequence during the forward pass. We propose Saliency-Weighted Asymmetric Merging (SWAM), a training-based token merging framework that extends the Bipartite Soft Matching (BSM) with two saliency-aware mechanisms. We introduce a two-step matching formulation in which cosine similarity decides candidate pairs, while a multiplicative maximum saliency penalty regulates their selection for merging. We then further use asymmetric exponential saliency-weighted aggregation, which allows more salient tokens to contribute more strongly to the merged representation. A lightweight MLP-based saliency prediction module (75k parameters per stage, 1% of backbone parameters) supervised via attention rollout is trained end-to-end jointly with a DeiT-Small backbone using a composite cross-entropy, knowledge-distillation, and saliency-alignment objective. On CIFAR-100, TinyImageNet, and ImageNet-100, under a conservative schedule that reduces tokens from 196 to 100 patch tokens, with the CLS token retained throughout, 27.5% FLOPs reduction and 1.35 times speedup, SWAM matches or exceeds baseline across the reported results. Under an aggressive schedule (196 to 70 tokens with the CLS token kept throughout, 33.8% FLOPs reduction, and 1.46 times speedup), accuracy gains are achieved on ImageNet-100 (+0.23%) with minimal losses on CIFAR-100 and TinyImageNet.

title: Few-Shot Open-Set Hyperspectral Pixel-Wise Classification with Spatial Aware Label Propagation
abstract: Pixelwise classification of hyperspectral images (HSI) is a fundamental task in remote sensing, but its deployment in real-world applications is often limited by the scarcity of labeled data and the presence of unknown classes at inference time. In this work, we propose Few-shot Open-set hyperspectral recognition from Self-Supervised Learning training (FOSSeL), a unified framework for few-shot, open-set hyperspectral pixelwise classification that does not require supervised training. The proposed approach first leverages self-supervised learning to construct a discriminative feature space from unlabeled data. Then, given a small set of labeled seed pixels, class predictions are obtained through spatially-aware graph-based label propagation over superpixel representations, enabling the joint exploitation of spectral similarity and spatial consistency. To address the open-set scenario, we introduce simple yet effective strategies to identify pixels that do not belong to the known classes. We evaluate FOSSeL on three benchmark hyperspectral datasets under multiple few-shot settings. The results show that the proposed framework achieves competitive or superior performance compared to fully supervised methods while maintaining robustness in the presence of unknown classes. These findings highlight the potential of combining self-supervised feature learning with graph-based inference for practical HSI analysis in low-annotation and open-world scenarios.

title: From Images to Grounded Edits: A Real-World Benchmark for Chinese Grammatical Error Correction in Handwritten Essays
abstract: Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (CGEC) is typically formulated as a text-to-text problem. While suitable for digital texts, this formulation falls short in real-world K-12 education, where AI-assisted corrections are expected directly on essay images, which are primarily handwritten and exhibit many irregularities. To bridge this gap, we introduce Grounded Chinese Grammatical Error Correction (G-CGEC), an image-to-grounded-edit task requiring systems to predict both corrections and their positions on essay images. We propose G-CGEC-Eval, a benchmark comprising real-world images of K-12 Chinese essays with fine-grained annotations. For evaluation, we adapt IoU-based metrics from object detection and propose a more tolerant alternative based on center-distance matching. Using this benchmark, we evaluate open-source and proprietary vision-language models under a direct single-pass setting, as well as settings with auxiliary components (OCR and character grounding) coordinated via pipelining or agentic harnessing. Results show that even top-tier proprietary models perform surprisingly poorly in the single-pass setting, while pipelining and agentic harnessing yield meaningful improvements. Notably, an error-type-based multi-agent workflow achieves the best performance, establishing it as the strongest baseline for future G-CGEC research. Through ablations and fine-grained analysis, we find the task remains far from solved, with linguistic error discovery and character-level grounding as the primary bottlenecks. This underscores the need for models that better integrate visual perception with linguistic reasoning and visual grounding.

title: nnAEU: a Simple and Efficient CNN-Autoencoder for Hyperspectral Unmixing
abstract: Deep learning-based hyperspectral unmixing (HSU) has followed a trajectory of increasing architectural complexity, from simple autoencoders to transformers and, most recently, Mamba-based models, each claiming to advance the state of the art. Contrary to this trend, we propose a lightweight CNN-based autoencoder, coined "Not New Autoencoder Unmixing" (nnAEU). It is derived from the backbone of UNMamba (2025) through a pruning study that removes the Mamba component entirely. nnAEU uses less than 10 times fewer parameters than UNMamba, and far fewer than other transformer- and GAN-based methods, while outperforming them in accuracy. We provide a complete, minimal, reproducible code, available at https://gitlab.telecom-paris.fr/ring/nnAEU.git.

title: See and Detect: Image-Driven Open-Vocabulary Multi-View 3D Object Detection
abstract: Recent open-vocabulary multi-view indoor 3D detection methods typically follow a point-cloud-driven pipeline, where pseudo 3D boxes are generated from reconstructed or estimated geometry and semantic labels are inferred from projected regions. However, such a design makes box generation dependent on the completeness of point clouds and restricts semantic learning to local appearance, causing inferior 3D object localization and open-vocabulary classification. In this paper, we present See and Detect, an image-driven framework that uses multi-view images as the primary evidence for 3D box and semantic label generation. For box generation, we first discover object candidates from individual images, enabling objects missing in point clouds to be recovered from visual evidence. However, single-view predictions are often noisy and redundant. To address this, we propose multi-view consensus box consolidation to fuse spatially consistent predictions across views, and box quality assessment to reduce the impact of boxes with partial object coverage. For semantic label generation, we introduce context-aware semantic learning, where semantic labels are queried from full image context, enabling more accurate semantic prediction. Extensive experiments on ScanNet and ARKitScenes demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art open-vocabulary multi-view 3D detection performance while running over 500$\times$ faster than the previous state-of-the-art method.

title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1). AstroVink-TREX: Automated strong gravitational lens segmentation as input for mass modelling pipelines
abstract: Strong gravitational lens modelling requires the lens light, lensed source light, and contaminants to be separated in each image before mass modelling codes can fit the system. Within Euclid this separation has so far been done by hand, which does not scale to the more than 15,000 candidates in the Euclid Lens Identification Pipeline and Scientific Exploration (ECLIPSE) catalogue of Data Release 1 (DR1). We present AstroVink-TREX , a neural network that performs this separation automatically and predicts three flux maps, in a standard format directly usable by mass-modelling pipelines. The network uses a hybrid architecture, pairing a vision transformer encoder reused from the lens detection network with a parallel convolutional branch. A custom loss function penalises both flux and structural error, while allowing independent weighting per component. From the network's predictions we also derive the modelling centre, fitting region, conjugate points, and binary maps, providing all the inputs that a modelling pipeline needs to run without manual setup. We evaluate the efficiency of the network on DR1 systems against existing fits and through expert validation. Across approximately 3000 inspected systems, taking 75% agreement between inspectors, just 39 lens models fail because of a segmentation error. Following this validation, the network provides the component separation and modelling setup for every system modelled in DR1. With automated segmentation, lens modelling is no longer limited by manual preprocessing and can now operate at the same scale as lens discovery.

title: Can Large Language Models Optimize Pretrained Neural Network Weights? A Multi-Phase Empirical Evaluation of Gradient-Free Editing in YOLO26 Object Detection
abstract: Direct weight editing offers a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning pretrained detectors, but its generalization and the value of large language model (LLM) guidance remain uncertain. We evaluate five experimental phases using YOLO26 models and MS COCO, comparing deterministic scaling, random perturbations, differential evolution, CMA-ES, structured interventions, real local-LLM proposals, failure-aware guidance, and hybrid LLM-CMA-ES against a matched random-policy control. Optimization uses native Ultralytics mAP50-95 on 1,000 COCO Val2017 images; selected candidates are assessed on a disjoint, previously examined 1,500-image subset, with COCO API AP50-95 reported separately where available. Increasing the CMA-ES budget from 8 to 250 evaluations raised development gains from +0.11 to +0.28 percentage points, while selection changes remained negative (-0.03 to -0.12 points); the 250-evaluation result uses one seed. The hybrid LLM approach showed no statistically established advantage over random-policy guidance (p = 0.612, 0.369, and 0.694 at budgets 8, 25, and 50). Five-seed YOLO26m replication yielded a COCO API AP difference of +0.004 points (95% CI: -0.026 to +0.034). Of 225 archived LLM proposals, 53 satisfy the final strict schema; early tensor-level execution cannot be fully verified. Genuine LLM-mediated weight editing is feasible, but the tested approaches did not demonstrate consistent transfer beyond the development subset or a measurable LLM advantage.

title: A novel approach for soil moisture retrieval via fusing multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations in entire Tibetan Plateau
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Spaceborne GNSS-Reflectometry (GNSS-R) is a powerful technology for soil moisture (SM) retrieval. However, complex topography and steep slopes over the Tibetan Plateau lead to significant signal loss and sampling sparsity. This study proposes a novel Dirichlet-prior-guided Vision Transformer (DG-ViT) framework to fuse multi-source observations from CYGNSS, Tianmu-1, and the FY-3E/F/G constellation. The novel DG-ViT framework incorporates land cover informed prior guidance into multi-spaceborne surface reflectivity (SR) fusion, and its performance is evaluated against single-source retrievals and traditional machine learning algorithms. To assess generalization, the fused SR was coupled with six mainstream machine learning algorithms (RF, XGBoost, ANN, BP, SVM, and GBDT) for 9 km daily SM retrieval, with multi-scale validation conducted against ERA5 SM and nine in-situ stations. Results demonstrate that the DG-ViT framework achieves a daily SR coverage of 89.49 %, representing an improvement of 20.13 % and 14.32 % over standalone CYGNSS and Tianmu-1 data, respectively. In addition, this fusion strategy overcomes the coverage gap of CYGNSS north of 38°N and compensates for the inability of individual FY-3 missions to support daily SM retrieval. In comparative assessments, the DG-ViT combined with RF yields superior performance (R = 0.955, RMSE = 0.039 cm 3 /cm 3 , bias = 0.000 cm 3 /cm 3 ), markedly enhancing retrieval accuracy relative to results derived from single-source CYGNSS or Tianmu-1 SR. In-situ validation shows ubRMSE values between 0.0232 and 0.0619 cm 3 /cm 3 , a 15.1 % precision gain over ERA5 SM. The proposed DG-ViT combined with RF approach effectively exploits the complementarity among multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations over the entire Tibetan Plateau, thereby compensating for the signal deficiencies of individual missions. This fusion approach provides a novel perspective for SM retrieval in high-altitude areas, specifically improving daily SR coverage and SM retrieval accuracy through fusion of multi-spaceborne GNSS-R observations with land cover informed prior guidance.

title: ObsGate-SST: observation-gated background–detail learning for global daily sea surface temperature reconstruction
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Infrared cloud screening and incomplete sampling limit the process-scale use of daily satellite sea surface temperature (SST), whereas many gap-filled Level-4 analyses attenuate narrow fronts, tropical-cyclone cold wakes and short-lived warm extremes. This study presents ObsGate-SST, an observation-gated background–detail learning framework for global daily SST reconstruction. The model ingests cloud-contaminated ODYSSEA L3S SST, a valid-pixel mask and an OISST v2.1 prior. A low-frequency branch estimates the basin-scale thermal background, a high-frequency branch reconstructs gradient and texture residuals from observed pixels, and a deterministic observation gate copies all valid satellite observations exactly so that inference is restricted to missing open-ocean pixels. Training used 2000–2020 daily fields, validation used 2021–2022 and independent testing used 2023–2025. Against 2023 quality-level-5 iQuam matchups, monthly bias ranged from 0.193 to 0.291 °C, RMSE from 0.637 to 0.849 °C and correlation from 0.993 to 0.996 across 902,665 collocations. A cloud-gap-shaped withheld-observed-pixel audit isolated inferred-pixel skill: ObsGate-SST achieved the lowest pooled RMSE (0.4802 °C), while removing the low-frequency branch, high-frequency branch, gradient/detail loss and physical/prior regularization increased RMSE by 17.0 %, 9.9 %, 3.9 % and 2.0 %, respectively. Relative to DINEOF, U-Net, Swin-Unet and SegNet under common masks, ObsGate-SST better retained spectral energy, frontal continuity, marine-heatwave structure, typhoon cold wakes and equatorial Pacific gradients. These results support observation-gated multiscale learning as a physically interpretable strategy for reconstructing incomplete satellite SST without sacrificing observed-pixel fidelity.

title: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 responses to Hansen-reported forest loss in the Peruvian Amazon: Timing and spatial sensitivity
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
abstract: Satellite signals preceding recorded tropical forest loss are rarely tested against locations without loss. We compared the timing of Sentinel-1 co-polarised (VV) and cross-polarised (VH) backscatter and three Sentinel-2 indices (Normalized Burn Ratio, NBR; Normalized Difference Moisture Index, NDMI; Normalized Difference Red Edge index, NDRE) with Hansen Global Forest Change loss years in the Ucayali Region of the Peruvian Amazon (2019–2025). Hansen loss years served as an annual, satellite-derived reference rather than independent ground truth. Monthly time series at 819 locations with Hansen loss in 2021–2024 at the central 30 m pixel were compared with 2,588 non-loss locations using before-after analysis, superposed epoch analysis and single-change-point breakpoint detection with a pseudo-year null model. Sensitivity to spatial matching was tested with 50–250 m buffers, and canopy height from the Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation was examined exploratorily. All variables declined around the Hansen loss year relative to non-loss locations, most strongly for Sentinel-2 (Cliff’s δ = − 0.66 to − 0.76; Sentinel-1: −0.27 to − 0.30). Negative breakpoints occurred at 74–82% of loss locations for the Sentinel-2 indices, mostly in the loss year. Breakpoints preceding the loss year occurred at 9.5–19.0% of loss locations, exceeding the non-loss comparison only for NBR (+4.9 percentage points) and NDRE (+3.8) at the primary penalty. Apparent pre-loss rates increased with buffer size and depended on breakpoint selection, and exploratory GEDI analysis found no detectable association between canopy height and breakpoint timing. Pre-loss satellite signals should be tested against non-loss baselines before being interpreted as early warning.

title: Integrating vegetation phenology and SWOT-derived surface water dynamics for improved county-scale winter wheat yield prediction
abstract: Winter wheat yield is shaped by crop growth status and surface hydrological conditions. However, remote-sensing approaches based primarily on vegetation index (VI) time series may not fully represent the surrounding surface-water environment in county-scale yield prediction. We integrated growth-stage VI features with surface-water dynamics derived from the Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) mission to predict county-level winter wheat yield in Henan Province, China. We evaluated direct feature fusion, same-year residual correction, and target-year residual correction following cross-year VI extrapolation using outer ten-fold cross-validation. Inner five-fold cross-fitting generated same-year VI residual targets exclusively within each outer training set. The VI-only model achieved R2 = 0.772, RMSE = 0.688 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.510 t ha−1. Direct incorporation of SWOT features reduced predictive accuracy, with R2 = 0.749, RMSE = 0.721 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.547 t ha−1. By contrast, SWOT-based residual correction yielded a clearer improvement in same-year prediction, increasing R2 to 0.795 and reducing RMSE to 0.652 t ha−1. The historical VI model was trained on 2010–2021, independently tested on 2022–2023, and extrapolated to 2024, where it achieved R2 = 0.676, RMSE = 0.819 t ha−1, and MAE = 0.611 t ha−1. Calibrated using observed 2024 yields from training counties and evaluated on held-out 2024 counties, subsequent target-year residual correction with concurrent SWOT features increased R2 to 0.749 and reduced RMSE and MAE to 0.722 and 0.524 t ha−1, respectively. SHAP analysis showed that SWOT contributions were concentrated during seeding, emergence, overwintering, green, heading–flowering, and filling and varied by spatial scale and prediction scenario. Overall, SWOT-derived surface-water observations provided complementary predictive information relative to the evaluated VI baselines, particularly for target-year spatial calibration. Their broader applicability across regions, crops, and years remains to be established through independent validation.

title: Person Recognition at Altitude and Range: Fusion of Face, Body Shape and Gait
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: We address the problem of whole-body person recognition in unconstrained environments. This problem arises in surveillance scenarios such as those in the IARPA Biometric Recognition and Identification at Altitude and Range (BRIAR) program, where biometric data is captured at long standoff distances, elevated viewing angles, and under adverse atmospheric conditions (e.g., turbulence and high wind velocity). To this end, we propose FarSight, a unified end-to-end system for person recognition that integrates complementary biometric cues across face, gait, and body shape modalities. FarSight comprises four core modules: multi-subject detection and tracking, recognition-aware video restoration, modality-specific biometric feature encoding, and quality-guided multi-modal fusion. Rather than treating these modules as independent processing stages, FarSight coordinates key stage-level decisions around the final biometric objective: tracking maintains identity-consistent temporal evidence, restoration is selectively invoked and optimized for recognition, and modality-quality estimates guide score fusion. This coordinated design supports recognition under degraded image conditions, large pose and scale variations, and cross-domain gaps. Extensive experiments on the BRIAR dataset, one of the most comprehensive benchmarks for long-range, multi-modal biometric recognition, demonstrate the effectiveness of FarSight. Compared with our preliminary system [1] on the Face-Included treatment set of BRIAR EVP 5.0.1, the current system improves 1:1 verification (TAR@0.1% FAR) by 34.4 percentage points and closed-set identification (Rank-20) by 17.8 percentage points, while reducing open-set identification errors (FNIR@1% FPIR) by 34.3 percentage points. Furthermore, FarSight was evaluated in the 2025 NIST RTE Face in Video Evaluation (FIVE), which conducts standardized face recognition testing on the BRIAR dataset. These results establish FarSight as a state-of-the-art solution for operational biometric recognition in challenging real-world conditions.

title: Representation of Directed Acyclic Graphs by Sequences of Instructions for Symbolic Regression
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Symbolic Regression (SR) aims to discover a closed-form mathematical expression that fits an observed dataset by representing those expressions as Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAGs). A DAG with k internal nodes admits Θ(k!) equivalent node orderings of the same expression, so structurally identical candidates repeatedly reach the fitness evaluator of the solver model, consuming search budget. We introduce ISALSR (Instruction Set and Language for Symbolic Regression), an encoding that maps every labeled DAG to a canonical string over a two-tier alphabet of structural and operation-labeled tokens. Canonical strings are reached via a greedy algorithm guided by 1-Weisfeiler-Leman (1-WL) subtree hashing. We prove that the canonical string is a complete labeled-DAG invariant under a reachability condition: two expressions share their string if and only if their DAGs are isomorphic. ISALSR integrates at the evaluation boundary and needs no change to the host search algorithm. It has been validated on a systematic enumerator (UDFS) and an evolutionary search (Bingo) over a 70-problem suite assembled from nine published benchmarks, against both the host solvers' native representation and a naive hash of a fixed-order DAG serialization. Canonicalization eliminates a mean of 38.1% of evaluations on UDFS and 43.7% on Bingo, on every one of the 70 problems under both hosts. A paired test across problems puts its reduction factor above that of the naive hash at a Cohen's d of 2.54 and 7.05, both at p < 10-12. Canonicalization consumes 0.04% of run time on UDFS and 16.1% on Bingo. Deduplication is therefore close to free where a fitness evaluation costs orders of magnitude more than a canonical string, and expensive where the two are comparable. ISALSR is the first instruction-based graph encoding to carry operation labels, edge direction and a non-commutative operator, and because the canonical form is itself a string, it also gives sequence models a target that is invariant to node renumbering. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/MarioPasc/IsalSR.

title: A Simple but Efficient Method to Achieve High Performance with Extreme Sparsity
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Pruning effectively removes redundant parameters and computations from neural networks, reduces model storage space, and saves time, memory, and energy during the training and inference phases. However, current pruning methods perform well at moderate and high sparsity, but the performance difference with dense network models at extreme sparsity is huge. In order to bridge the accuracy gap between extremely sparse and dense models, this paper proposes a simple but efficient pruning strategy-Tensor Decomposition Based Iterative Magnitude Pruning (TDIMP) method. This strategy uses tensor theory to optimize the model structure before IMP to reduce the search space of the sparse subnetwork during pruning, thus improving the hit rate of the optimal sparse subnetwork. Specifically, firstly, the weight matrix or weight tensor of the dense model is represented as a low-rank tensor decomposition format, and the feature extraction capability of the base module is enhanced by multi-step chaining operations to construct a low-rank compact network model. Secondly, IMP is performed on the low-rank model. The weight updates are sampled multiple times at the later stages of model training during each magnitude pruning process to smooth the oscillations of the learning trajectory and improve the performance of the sparse model. To evaluate the superiority of TDIMP, we first conducted extensive experiments using LSTM, VGGNet, ResNet, and Transformer architectures on UCF11, CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet, and ImageNet datasets at sparsities ranging from 98% to 99.9%, and compared it with state-of-the-art methods.
