Experimental results show that TDIMP has higher accuracy, faster inference and less storage space than the pruning at initialization, dynamic sparse training, and iterative pruning methods in the extreme sparse case. In addition, TDIMP also has faster training speed than IMP methods.

title: 2D Gaussian Splatting for Semantic Segmentation via Discrete-to-Continuous Representation toward Boundary-Preserving Feature Upsampling
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: High-quality semantic segmentation requires not only rich semantic understanding but also precise delineation of object boundaries. While prevailing methods rely on discrete feature representations that often lead to boundary misalignment, jagged contours, and blurry edges along complex contours, we present GSSeg, a novel semantic segmentation paradigm based on Gaussian Splatting that has been successfully applied to 3D scene reconstruction. Specifically, GSSeg reformulates the discrete feature space as continuous Gaussian fields, thereby rendering spatial continuity modeling to produce high-quality segmentation results. However, directly adapting 2DGS to existing pipelines suffers from the structural granularity loss in low-resolution features and the inherent low-pass limitations of Gaussian rendering. To address the insufficient structural granularity available for discrete-to-continuous transformation, we propose the cross-layer neighborhood interaction scheme utilizing alternating global scanning, which establishes cross-scale contextual cues to enhance adaptive Gaussian kernel generation. Additionally, addressing the inherent low-pass limitations of Gaussian rendering, we introduce spatial uncertainty-aware resampling driven by resolution bias estimation, which selectively compensates for high-frequency details attenuated during Gaussian rendering. Furthermore, we introduce an effective Gaussian kernel initialization strategy that approximates Gaussian radial basis function interpolation, ensuring model training stability. Comprehensive experiments on standard benchmarks, especially high-resolution matting-level dataset MaSS13K, demonstrate that GSSeg achieves state-of-the-art performance.

title: Seeing Text Clearly in the Dark: Unifying Localization and Enhancement via Deep Morphological Synergy
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Low-light text localization, an interdisciplinary field, has gained significant attention recently. The goal is to provide enhanced text locational information beneficial for both machine and human vision. Existing one-stage and two-stage methods either rely on single detectors specially designed for low-light conditions or on a simple cascade of detectors and enhancers, both of which exhibit limitations in effectively addressing the joint task of enhancement and text localization simultaneously. Relying solely on a single set of dual operations in deep morphology, we link the joint task via a bidirectional morphological sync bridge that ensures the simultaneous flow of two directions: one preserving the topological connectivity of text and the other improving its exposure level under low-light conditions. We then introduce a novel bi-level synergistic learning strategy, where text localization serves as the upper-level task and enhancement as the lower-level task. This strategy leverages bidirectional connectivity in the deep morphological sync bridge as a learnable constraint and alternately updates coupled gradients with different update frequencies to optimize the joint task. Extensive experiments on the low-light text localization dataset LATeD demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art techniques in both tasks. The code will be released.

title: Kernel Adaptive Deformable Convolution for Remote Sensing Object Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Modeling geometric variations, particularly the extreme fluctuations in scale and shape, stands as a persistent challenge in computer vision, which is significantly exacerbated in remote sensing object detection (RSOD). Existing methods are often constrained by the fixed geometric topology of standard convolutions or the insufficient representation power of linear feature aggregation, making it difficult to strike an ideal balance between adaptability and computational efficiency. To address these challenges, we propose a novel scale- and shape-adaptive method named Kernel Adaptive Deformable Convolution (KAD-Conv). Specifically, KAD-Conv employs a specialized Deformable Spatial Convolution (DSC) at its core to adaptively adjust sampling locations, while reformulating the mask generation process to fully leverage the mask's potential for discriminative feature modulation. In KAD-Conv, we further introduce a Scale-aware Kernel Adaptive mechanism, which enables the dynamic adjustment of sampling scales to effectively capture object representations across extreme scale variations without increasing kernel size. With KAD-Conv, we develop a novel object detection network based on Multi-task Guided Learning (MGL), called KAD-CNet. Extensive experiments conducted on widely used remote sensing benchmark datasets, including DOTA-v1.0, DIOR, and NWPU VHR-10, along with validation on natural scenes exhibiting extreme geometric variations, have validated the effectiveness of the proposed KAD-CNet. Moreover, comprehensive comparisons against various YOLO-series models further underscore the practical value and efficiency of the proposed approach.

title: GenHOI: Generalizing Text-driven 4D Human-Object Interaction Synthesis for Unseen Objects
HENet++: Hybrid Encoding and Multi-task Learning for 3D Perception and Planning in Autonomous Driving
Dynamic Knowledge-Aware for Streaming View Clustering
abstract: In real scenarios, multi-view data are often continuously acquired in the form of view streams, giving rise to the task of Streaming View Clustering (SVC). However, most existing methods rely on view-specific knowledge to guide the learning of the current view, while neglecting the shared, view-invariant knowledge structure across views. As a result, the model progressively forgets the commonalities between current and historical views during training, i.e., catastrophic forgetting, which leads to severe fluctuations in clustering performance under different input sequences. To address this issue, we propose a Dynamic kNowledge-Aware (DNA) framework for SVC, which is designed to mitigate the negative impact of catastrophic forgetting effectively. The proposed DNA framework consists of two main stages: the initial learning stage and the continual learning stage. Specifically, during the initial learning stage, we employ knowledge-aware learning to extract prototype knowledge from the first acquired view and construct an initial knowledge base. During the continual learning stage, we leverage knowledge aggregation learning to maximize the consistency between the prototype knowledge of the current view and the historical knowledge, and then fuse them into a new prototype knowledge and update the knowledge base, thereby ensuring the completeness of the learned knowledge. Finally, through structural guidance learning, the updated knowledge base is used to steer the sample distribution of the current view, thereby ensuring distributional consistency across different views. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that DNA consistently and significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods. The code is available at https://github.com/hl-yuan/DNA.

title: Degradation-aware Infrared Image Super-Resolution
abstract: Infrared image super-resolution (IISR) is inherently more challenging than its visible-light counterpart due to the presence of structured, infrared-specific degradations, including thermal noise, fixed-pattern noise, and spatially non-uniform blur. These degradations deviate substantially from commonly assumed degradation models and often lead existing methods to produce unstable structures, amplified noise, or hallucinated textures. In this work, we present DIRSR, a degradation-aware framework for infrared image super-resolution that explicitly incorporates infrared degradation perception into the restoration process. The proposed approach characterizes instance-level infrared degradation conditions and leverages degradation-aware semantic guidance to regulate the trade-off between perceptual quality and structural fidelity. In addition, infrared imaging priors are embedded into a physics-informed, region-aware optimization objective to enhance foreground structural consistency while suppressing spurious background details. Extensive experiments on multiple public infrared benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both quantitative performance and visual quality, and further improves downstream infrared detection and segmentation tasks.

title: STRIDE: Continual Learning using Skill Transfer and Reuse with Incremental Discrete Encoding
abstract: Developing general-purpose physics-based character controllers via reinforcement learning is fundamentally hindered by policy interference in continuous spaces. While training isolated controllers avoids interference, it incurs significant training overhead and yields disjointed behavioral transitions. To address these challenges, we present STRIDE (Skill Transfer and Reuse with Incremental Discrete Encoding), a framework for the continual learning and composition of diverse character behaviors. Instead of training independent models, STRIDE leverages policy quantization via a Vector Quantized Variational Autoencoder (VQ-VAE) to dynamically discover and encode reusable behavioral primitives within a discrete latent space. New behaviors and tasks are learned by combining existing codewords, providing a stable motion prior that structurally eliminates catastrophic forgetting. Evaluated across diverse locomotion styles, agile maneuvers like kicking, and composite tasks like target-aiming, STRIDE accelerates downstream learning by × 1.3 to × 2.0 compared to baseline learning frameworks. Furthermore, the discrete representations inherently improve policy interpretability, allowing direct tracking of skill activations and behavioral decisions during task execution. STRIDE offers a scalable, transparent solution for continual character control without compromising motion quality.

title: Resilient Transmission of Highly Structured Light via Active Convolved Illumination
abstract: Wave propagation through lossy and noisy systems as well as spatiotemporally dynamic random media often limits the complex information that can be reliably transmitted or retrieved. Progress in adaptive optics, wavefront shaping, machine learning, and wave propagation theories has significantly advanced physical and computational correction techniques. However, many approaches remain constrained by restrictive operating conditions, limiting their ability to meet growing application-specific demands, such as higher spatial resolution in imaging and greater data capacity in communications, particularly in highly dynamic environments. Recently, active convolved illumination (ACI) was proposed as a novel framework for preserving the spatial structure of optical modes during propagation through strongly distorting environments, such as atmospheric turbulence. ACI aims to bypass the prohibitive complexity of global distortion tracking by combining spectrally localized characterization with compensation using a correlated auxiliary source. Here, we provide a comprehensive review of ACI, detailing the formulation of correlation-injecting and auxiliary sources and the role of segmented reciprocal-space characterization and distortion compensation. We explore extensions in free-space optical communication and potential high-precision phase measurement, and numerically evaluate interferometric strategies for experimental implementation. This work highlights ACI as a potentially versatile framework for distortion-resilient light transmission, with broad interdisciplinary utility ranging from atmospheric physics and remote sensing to telecommunications, target tracking, and biomedical diagnosis, offering flexible deployment either as a standalone paradigm or hybridized with existing optical systems.

title: Objects as Addresses: Instance Binding in Vision Transformer Attention
abstract: Humans naturally parse visual scenes into coherent individual objects rather than scattered features, a capability cognitive science calls object binding. While recent work shows that pretrained Vision Transformers (ViTs) intrinsically acquire this ability, how native self-attention computations mechanistically keep object instances separate remains unresolved. By studying this across eight pretrained ViTs, we found that instance separation is expressed more strongly in attention routing than in token content: selected query-key relations distinguish individual objects more reliably than value similarity or residual representations. Inside heads, patches belonging to one individual tend to read from a common image region, which we term their attention address. Visually distinct parts of one person share an address, whereas identical duplicated instances receive separate, movable addresses. These shared destinations arise in part because query interactions with the spatial structure of keys direct attention toward consistent regions for one object and elsewhere for another. In DINOv2 and most other backbones we tested, editing this query component at the selected head redirects its attention address toward another individual. Grouping patches by this query component separates same-category instances, reaching .615 FG-ARI versus .289 for the same clustering of final-layer features, which tend to merge them.

title: MALNISI-Infused Graph Construction and Weighted Contrastive Loss based GAT for Unsupervised Representation Learning in HSI
abstract: Hyperspectral images (HSI) possess discriminating spectral characteristics with respect to land utilization due to high-dimensional information. Recently, unsupervised representation learning using graph neural networks has unveiled these utilization-specific complex spectral relations. This article has three main contributions. First, it proposes an index, the Mean Absolute Local Neighborhood Inverse Spectral Index (MALNISI), which measures the similarity between two pixels based on their neighborhood information. The index is used to construct a weighted adjacency matrix, giving the HSI a graph structure. Second, it proposes an upgraded Graph Attention Network that learns compact latent representations of hyperspectral data from the constructed graph. In this network, an enhanced multi-head attention mechanism incorporates the MALNISI weights as an auxiliary feature to emphasize learned attention between neighboring pixels. To alleviate over-smoothing and preserve fine-grained spectral details, the architecture integrates residual connections, skip projections, and feature normalization, which together enhance representation capability, stabilize learning, and accelerate convergence. Third, it proposes a weighted contrastive loss function that incorporates neighborhood-aware MALNISI between connected pixels, encouraging strongly connected pixels in the high-dimensional space to remain close in the latent space, and weakly connected pixels to stay apart. The resulting discriminative low-dimensional embeddings are then clustered using spectral clustering. Experimental analysis on six benchmark HSI datasets demonstrates the efficiency and necessity of the three aforementioned contributions, and the comparative study highlights superior performance over fourteen state-of-the-art approaches.

title: SpotDiff: A Plug-and-Play Framework for Zero-Shot Change Detection in Remote Sensing Imagery
abstract: Remote sensing change detection usually relies on large collections of temporally aligned, pixel-level annotations, which limits its scalability across regions, imaging platforms and application domains. Recent zero-shot approaches reduce the need for supervision, but they often localize fine-grained changes poorly because their features are coarse or inconsistent across time. We present SpotDiff, a training-free, plug-and-play framework for zero-shot change detection built by composing complementary vision foundation models. SpotDiff uses DINOv3 for semantically robust features, AnyUp to reconstruct them at pixel resolution, and SAM 3 for text-guided region-of-interest proposals, which an inference-time multi-scale strategy (SWIMS) makes reliable on small objects. Change is then measured by comparing the reconstructed features of the two dates inside the proposed regions, with no learnable components, fine-tuning or change labels. To our knowledge, SpotDiff is the first change detection method to use a universal feature upsampler, which alone adds 13.8 F1 over bilinear upsampling of the same features. On LEVIR-CD, SpotDiff reaches 82.46 F1, 2.06 points above the strongest prior training-free method, and on the multi-class SECOND benchmark it improves building change detection by 10.3 IoU and the six-class average by 2.2 IoU. Qualitative results on PlanetScope (3 m) and Sentinel-2 (10 m) imagery show that the same pipeline transfers across resolutions without modification. Our results indicate that composing modern foundation models is an effective route to scalable, label-free change detection.

title: SALT: State-Aligned Low-Rank Transfer for Single-Temporal Cross-Dataset Structural Localization in Remote Sensing
abstract: Change detection in remote sensing conventionally relies on spatially aligned bi-temporal imagery, which may be unavailable or unreliable in practical scenarios. Recent single-temporal approaches address this limitation by learning structural evidence, such as building regions, from a labeled source dataset and transferring it to unseen target imagery using only the current image. However, adaptation to the source dataset can over-specialize pretrained features and reduce their cross-dataset generalization, a risk that this paper argues is higher when the feature adaptation is parameterized independently of the states used for prediction. To address this issue, the current study introduces SALT, a State-Aligned Low-Rank Transfer framework. SALT keeps a DINOv3 backbone frozen and learns negative and positive structural states that both score each patch and, through State-Aligned Low-Rank Adaptation (SALA), span the rank-2 subspace in which patch features are corrected. Directional State Alignment supervises these corrections to raise the evidence of positive patches and lower that of negative ones, while Geometry Preservation limits changes to the pairwise relations among pretrained patch features. Experiments on LEVIR-CD and the WHU aerial building dataset show that, at the pixel level and in both transfer directions, SALT outperforms four baselines reproduced under a common source-only protocol, improving over the strongest reproduced baselines by 9.45 and 5.79 points in pixel-level AP and by 27.69 and 14.25 points in IoU (LEVIR-CD to WHU and WHU to LEVIR-CD, respectively), with only 0.068M trainable parameters and 40.2 ms per image. In order to facilitate reproducibility and further research, the source code of SALT is available at https://github.com/gthpapadopoulos/SALT

title: Your Vision Foundation Model Is Secretly an EEG Foundation Model
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) foundation models are pretrained on thousands of hours of recordings, yet their frozen features transfer poorly to downstream tasks, and this transfer does not consistently improve with larger models or more pretraining data. We show that a vision foundation model that has never seen EEG is a stronger frozen EEG encoder than these specialized models, once the signals are rendered as images that a vision transformer can read. Our method, SeeEEG, keeps the vision backbone frozen and learns only how EEG is displayed to it. Each channel occupies a dedicated row of patches and is drawn either as a waveform at a fixed gain or as a scalogram whose frequency range spans the patch height, so that task-relevant patterns fall within individual tokens. The montage, filtering, and contrast parameters of this display are initialized from a standard clinical montage and optimized with the task loss through the frozen backbone, which amounts to at most 1,113 trainable parameters per view. We compare SeeEEG with seven EEG foundation models on eight clinical, sleep, affective, and brain-computer interface datasets, with every encoder frozen and paired with identical readout heads. With a frozen DINOv3 ViT-B, SeeEEG outperforms every EEG foundation model in balanced accuracy on all eight datasets and reaches a mean rank of 1.3 in Cohen kappa or AUROC, compared with 2.9 for the strongest baseline, REVE. The learned displays transfer without further optimization to the video encoder V-JEPA 2.1, which outperforms every EEG foundation model on both metrics on six of the eight datasets. Replacing DINOv3 with a randomly initialized ViT-B lowers the score by 15.2 points on average, so the ability to read rendered EEG comes from visual pretraining.

title: ElasticDino: Dense Semantic Features Using Elastic Deformations
abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) serve as the backbone for countless vision tasks, including dense prediction tasks, such as segmentation and depth estimation, even though the quadratic complexity of self-attention severely limits feature resolution and induces spatial artifacts. In this work, we introduce ElasticDino, a lightweight adapter which produces high-resolution feature maps, adhering to the fine details of the input image. As a key insight, we observe the consistency of artifacts across channels, and simultaneously resolve them to match the input image structure. Using a slim architecture based on spatial deformations, ElasticDino produces pixel-aligned, high-resolution feature maps efficiently. Leveraging deformations allows strictly preserving sharp semantics, and thereby avoiding the smoothness biases inherent to alternative approaches. Due to the absence of ground truth, we employ pixel-level semantic segmentation and depth estimation with linear heads to predict a set of downstream dense tasks, guiding the deformation process without leaking task-specific semantics into the model. We demonstrate superior accuracy over current methods on a range of popular dense task benchmarks, with better computational performance.

title: Report of the 8th LSVOS Challenge: Mobile Unified Multimodal Understanding
abstract: This report summarizes the Mobile Unified Multimodal Understanding (MUMU) track of the 8th Large-scale Video Object Segmentation (LSVOS) Challenge, held in conjunction with ECCV 2026. MUMU asks for a single unified model that jointly performs multi-concept image tagging over quality, scene, and event vocabularies, open-vocabulary object detection, and concise image captioning, within a budget of 0.5B parameters and 8 GB of peak inference memory. Submissions are ranked by a weighted task score scaled by an efficiency factor. We describe the tasks, rules, and evaluation protocol, report the final results, and review the methods of the top three teams. All three leading solutions build on the compact Florence-2-base model, but extend it in different ways: lightweight tagging heads with cross-task inference refinement, a shared low-rank adapter trained on coverage-aware multi-source data with task-dependent decoding, and a training-free pipeline that maps captions to tags and applies detection test-time augmentation. The results show that a compact prompt-based vision-language model can serve all three outputs when supervision, decoding, and cross-task cues are designed for each task, while open-vocabulary detection on novel categories remains the main bottleneck.

title: Third-Place Solution for the UCF UrbanTwin V2X-Real Track at ECCV 2026: Synthetic Point Cloud Generation and Sim-to-Real 3D Object Detection
abstract: This report presents a complete technical solution for the UrbanTwin V2X-Real Sim2Real LiDAR Challenge, covering both synthetic point cloud generation and 3D object detection. For data generation, we adopt per-axis quantile calibration. Public V2X-Real training data are used to construct the real reference distribution, and independent one-dimensional quantile mappings are estimated for the x, y, and z axes of the base synthetic point clouds. The calibrated point clouds are then resampled using a fixed random seed and clipped to the valid spatial range, producing 50 frames with 2,000 float32 XYZ points per frame. For detection, we use a two-stage Voxel R-CNN (VoxelRCNN) detector trained with RangeLDM-enhanced synthetic point-cloud data, point clouds downsampled to 50k points per frame, and reconstructed pedestrian data. Training is performed on four NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 GPUs with a global batch size of 16 for 40 epochs. Final testing uses direct single-model inference with the original VoxelRCNN model. On the official evaluation server, the normalized Realism score is 0.7905 and the normalized Detection score is 0.5583, with mAP@0.5 of 0.3908, BEV mAP@0.5 of 0.4219, and mAP@0.7 of 0.1047. According to the official weighting rule, the final combined score is 0.6 x 0.5583 + 0.4 x 0.7905 = 0.6512. This report documents the complete implementation details of data construction, model training, inference, submission formatting, and official evaluation.

title: Mitigating variance shrinkage in multi-task galaxy property inference from imaging data via statistical manifold alignment
abstract: Inferring photometric redshifts ($z$) and key stellar population properties ($\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $D_n4000$, and $\mathrm{H}δ_A$) directly from multi-band imaging is increasingly critical for spectroscopically limited large surveys such as LSST and CSST. However, conventional point-wise loss functions (e.g., mean squared error or Huber loss) employed in deep neural networks often induce ``variance shrinkage''---a regression-to-the-mean effect that contracts predicted variances, distorts non-linear physical manifolds (such as bimodal distributions), and truncates heavy-tail populations. Here, we present ViTMultiTask, a vision transformer framework that incorporates a multi-scale maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) loss to enforce higher-order joint distribution alignment in reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS). Trained on 83,846 galaxies from Subaru HSC five-band ($g,r,i,z,y$) imaging cross-matched with DESI Data Release 1 Bright Galaxy Survey spectra, the model achieves high point-estimate precision on an independent test set of 5,000 galaxies: $σ_{\mathrm{NMAD}} = 0.020$ for $z$, $0.169\,\mathrm{dex}$ for $\log(M_*/\mathrm{M}_\odot)$, $0.073$ for $D_n4000$, and $1.185\,\text{Å}$ for $\mathrm{H}δ_A$. Ablation experiments demonstrate that incorporating the MMD loss effectively mitigates variance shrinkage and more accurately reproduces the observed spectroscopic parameter distributions (including bimodal structures and heavy tails), while maintaining point-estimate accuracy statistically consistent with the baseline (RMSE changes $\le 3.5\%$) and catastrophic outlier rates fully comparable to the baseline. This kernel-based manifold alignment offers a statistically grounded and practical paradigm for comprehensive galaxy property inference in the deep imaging era.

title: RICapBench: A Fine-Grained Visual Understanding Benchmark Dataset for Vision-Language Models in Remote Sensing
abstract: Advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have improved remote sensing image analysis and supported geospatial decision-making. However, fine-grained understanding of remote sensing imagery remains challenging for VLMs. Large variations in object scale, complex geospatial relations among instances, and limited visual detail hinder precise instance localization, visible attribute identification, and spatial relation understanding, potentially leading to descriptions that lack visual grounding. Existing datasets and benchmarks insufficiently assess end-to-end instance localization and captioning without target-specific textual cues. To support this evaluation, we introduce RICapBench, a dataset and benchmark that unifies instance localization and fine-grained captioning in remote sensing. RICapBench contains 245,466 instance-level annotations and 498,005 spatial relation tuples spanning general remote sensing, UAV remote sensing, and dense small-object scenarios. Each annotation pairs an object's oriented bounding box with a natural language description of its visible attributes and spatial relations to surrounding instances and environmental elements. To evaluate the accuracy and completeness of spatial relation captioning, we propose a remote sensing spatial relation parser and the RelCap-F1 metric. We combine RelCap-F1 with instance localization and attribute captioning metrics into a composite metric, RICScore. Our evaluation of 15 advanced open-source and closed-source VLMs identifies instance localization as a major bottleneck for these models. LocateAnything achieves the highest RICScore of 31.68, but scores lower on spatial relation captioning than other task-fine-tuned open-source VLMs. Code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Xldln/RICapBench.

title: Gravity and Flight: Learning to Navigate Fine-Grained Remote Sensing Scenes
abstract: Vision-language models are increasingly capable, yet their reasoning in complex remote sensing scenes can remain coarse-grained and insufficiently grounded in task-relevant visual evidence. We propose Gravity and Flight (G&F), a framework for scene specialization with limited supervision that separates visual and reasoning verification while coupling policy updates. It combines Evidence-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning (EoT-SFT) and Relational Transfer Policy Optimization (RTPO). EoT-SFT teaches fine-grained observation and faithful reasoning through description, analysis, and supported conclusions. RTPO independently samples responses to scene-matched image pairs with fine-grained visual differences under a shared task. Its rubric-based verification combines Gravity, which checks visual fidelity and description coverage, and Flight, which takes descriptions as premises to assess evidence use and relations between paired judgments. Their scores and task correctness yield a shared pair-level advantage that couples policy updates from both responses. Using 1,008 demonstrations and 500 training pairs for harbor specialization, G&F achieves a mean score of 69.12 across six evaluation sets, exceeding the backbone and supervised initialization by 9.76 and 4.56 points. Matched controls show gains over single-image and joint-input RL, and removing either verification view reduces performance. Applying G&F to urban specialization also improves on the base model and supervised initialization across three evaluation subsets. Project details and updates are available at https://github.com/Z0ngL1ng/Gravity-and-Flight.

title: Uncertainty Aware AFM-IR Hyperspectral Cube Reconstruction via Convolutional-Attentive Conditional Neural Processes
abstract: Atomic force microscopy-infrared spectroscopy (AFM-IR) maps chemical composition at nanoscale spatial resolution, but the time required to acquire individual spectra limits hyperspectral imaging. Here, we introduce a convolutional-attentive conditional neural process (CACNP), a neural process architecture for reconstructing AFM-IR hyperspectral cubes from sparsely sampled spectra and a small set of structure images, each acquired at a selected wavenumber. The model is trained entirely on synthetic cubes generated from experimental infrared spectra and predicts both spectral intensities and their associated uncertainty. Validation on experimental datasets of poly(methyl methacrylate) and polystyrene particles embedded in epoxy demonstrates accurate reconstruction using only 5% of the available spectra, with competitive performance when compared to other methods. Inference takes less than 0.1 s on 128 X 128 hyperspectral cubes, supporting rapid reconstruction updates, while predictive uncertainty provides a basis for adaptive sampling of localized chemical features. This approach advances autonomous, high-throughput AFM-IR workflows and offers an architecture for accelerating other hyperspectral imaging methods.

title: A multi-sensor framework for comparing and integrating optical, C-band and L-band SAR inundation products in tropical floodplain of Australia
abstract: Accurate inundated landscape mapping is essential for understanding hydrological connectivity, wetland dynamics and floodplain processes in tropical environments. However, optical and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) sensors often produce inconsistent inundation estimates due to differences in sensor physics, wavelength sensitivity, vegetation and cloud penetration, and analytical methods. These challenges are amplified in wet–dry tropical systems, where cloud cover, heterogeneous vegetation and seasonal flooding complicate water detection. This study develops a unified multi-sensor framework for comparing and integrating inundation products derived from Sentinel-2 optical imagery, Sentinel-1 C-band and PALSAR-2 L-band SAR in the Daly River floodplain system in northern Australia. Inundated landscape maps were generated using supervised Random Forest classification and unsupervised multi-Otsu thresholding, followed by multi-sensor fusion analysis. Products were developed and validated using wet- and dry-season field observations and Indigenous Knowledges. Results showed strong seasonal and sensor-specific differences. Sentinel-2 provided the most balanced representation of dry-season floodplain vegetation and inundation, while Sentinel-1 achieved high wet-season overall accuracy (>0.95) under cloud-affected conditions. PALSAR-2 improved the detection of inundated vegetation and structurally complex environments, reaching an overall accuracy of 0.97. Multi-sensor evidential reasoning (fusion) improved spatial coherence and class delineation, but performance varied across sensor combinations. These findings show that optical, C-band SAR and L-band SAR inundation products are not directly interchangeable in tropical wetlands. Instead, they performed separately for each landscape. The proposed framework supports the comparison and integration of multi-sensor inundation products to enhance wetland conservation initiatives, wetland monitoring, hydrological assessment, and environmental management in data-limited tropical regions globally.

title: BathyUNet++ : a bathymetry retrieval framework for high-resolution low-SNR SuperDove imagery
abstract: High-spatial-resolution (HR) bathymetry is crucial for ensuring navigation safety and effective environmental management in shallow waters. However, traditional bathymetry retrieval from medium-resolution satellites yields large uncertainties under complex substrates and strong spatial heterogeneity. HR sensors, such as PlanetScope SuperDove (~3.7 m), can resolve fine-scale features but often have low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and limited spectral bands, leading to noisy bathymetry retrievals. To address this challenge, we developed BathyUNet++, a UNet++ architecture enhanced with spatial and channel squeeze & excitation (scSE) attention modules, for bathymetry retrieval from SuperDove imagery. While this architecture effectively leverages spatial context and complementary spectral information, it requires dense training patches. Traditional depth measurements provide sparse spatial coverage, and Airborne LiDAR Bathymetry (ALB) remains geographically limited. Therefore, we adopted a multi-source training strategy that integrates high-resolution ALB data with extensive Landsat 8/9 derived bathymetry to improve the spatial coverage and diversity of training data for SuperDove imagery. In addition, we designed a Central-Region Mean Squared Error (CMSE) that focuses on each patch's center valid receptive field to reduce instability and checkerboard artifacts often seen in satellite products generated via patch-based processing. Independent validation shows that BathyUNet++ achieves high-accuracy bathymetry retrievals, with median absolute percentage differences below 15% compared with independent depth measurements from ICESat-2 and ALB. Notably, BathyUNet++ substantially reduces noise compared with bathymetry maps derived from pixel-based algorithms, yielding spatially consistent bathymetry maps. The proposed framework overcomes the limitations of low-SNR data and can be readily adapted to other HR sensors, offering a promising solution for the broader application of HR bathymetry retrieval in optically shallow waters.

title: Vector Map as Language: Toward Unified Remote Sensing Vector Mapping
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Remote sensing vector mapping aims to generate structured maps of geospatial entities, such as buildings, roads, and water bodies, from remote sensing imagery. In practice, vector maps usually contain multiple category layers and heterogeneous entity structures, requiring a unified model for diverse mapping needs. However, existing methods typically represent vector objects as polygons or graphs, making them suitable only for specific categories: polygons poorly capture topological relations, while graphs often blur instance boundaries. We observe that language, as a natural medium for human communication, offers a flexible and expressive representation that can accommodate heterogeneous map elements, including geometry, semantics, and topology. Motivated by this insight, we propose Vector Map as Language (VecLang), a unified paradigm that reformulates multiclass vector mapping as structured text generation. VecLang encodes the common elements of different geospatial entities into a GeoJSON-like vector language, enabling cross-category modeling within a shared textual format. To generate this language reliably, we design a progressive vision-language mapping framework that first localizes vectorization units and then generates structured map elements. We further introduce Hierarchical Vector Language Optimization, which uses reinforcement learning to improve syntax validity, content fidelity, and map executability. We also build VecMap with 46k images and 800K instances, supporting training and evaluation across standard and generalization settings. Extensive experiments demonstrate that VecLang handles both single-class and multiclass vector mapping while achieving strong cross-dataset and open-vocabulary generalization.

title: TRUE: Towards Robust, Unique, and Efficient Model Fingerprint Generation and Verification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: While deep neural networks (DNNs) are being widely adopted, they are also increasingly exposed to model stealing risks, posing significant threats to intellectual property. Model fingerprinting, which utilizes intrinsic characteristics derived from the training process to authenticate models, has been proposed as a potential solution. An ideal fingerprint should satisfy robustness, uniqueness, and efficiency. However, existing methods often struggle to balance these three aspects simultaneously. To address this challenge, we propose TRUE, a twostage fingerprint generation and verification framework. In the fingerprint generation stage, we adopt adversarial examples as the fingerprint type and enhance their robustness through a minmax robust optimization strategy. In the fingerprint verification stage, we assign weights to the adversarial examples using a Boltzmann distribution to reflect their uniqueness, and further employ sampling based on these weights to reduce the number of queries and improve efficiency. Extensive experiments conducted on real-world datasets and across different model architectures demonstrate the superiority of the TRUE framework.

title: HPS-MVC: Hierarchical Pseudo-Supervised Multi-View Clustering
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Existing pseudo-supervised multi-view clustering methods typically utilize pseudo-supervision at a single semantic level, which fails to capture the intrinsic structure of complex data and thus restricts clustering performance. We propose Hierarchical Pseudo-Supervised Multi-View Clustering (HPS-MVC), which leverages multi-level semantic pseudo-supervision signals to guide the clustering process. Specifically, hierarchical pseudo-supervision signals are constructed by mining sample neighborhood relations and are then used to aggregate samples at different semantic levels as inputs to an anchor-based multi-view clustering model. A dual-weighting strategy is further introduced to select high-quality anchor graphs for optimal graph fusion. An efficient alternating optimization algorithm is developed to solve the resulting problem. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness, efficiency, and scalability of the proposed method.

title: Contextual Chamfer Distance for Point Cloud Restoration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Accurate similarity measurement between point clouds is crucial for 3D geometry restoration. Chamfer Distance (CD) and its variants quantify such similarity in a permutation-invariant manner, yet they emphasize low-order point-wise proximity, leading to clustered distributions and long-range structural distortions that undermine geometric fidelity. This work rethinks point cloud similarity from a high-order standpoint and introduces Contextual Chamfer Distance (CCD), a geometrically consistent formulation that jointly models point-wise proximity, local distribution consistency, and long-range structural consistency. Specifically, Patch Density Consistency (PDC) aligns relative patch densities between predicted and ground-truth points, promoting spatial coverage for geometric completeness, while Anchor Normal Consistency (ANC) models long-range relationships through anchor normals derived from non-degenerate point triplets, improving structural coherence and geometric accuracy. Alongside this formulation, we develop a conditional local coordinate-space stability and convergence analysis and derive sufficient conditions for local linear convergence of the corresponding weighted objective under explicit local assumptions. Extensive experiments on completion, compression, and upsampling across architectures and six datasets demonstrate consistent quantitative and qualitative gains across settings, a favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-off, and strong generalization.

title: Towards Robust Multi-View Clustering via Early-to-late Manifold Consistency Calibration
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: For multi-view data, structural heterogeneity across views is a common property, with cross-view sparsity variation serving as a typical manifestation. To first account for this sparsity-induced heterogeneity, we develop Adaptive View-specific Encoding, which incorporates the sparsity ratio of each view as prior knowledge for view-aware representation learning and constraint modulation. Based thereon, we further tackle the broader issue of view quality imbalance in multi-view fusion, where low-quality views introduce unreliable structural relations and view-specific constraints further amplify latent discrepancies. To this end, we propose a globallocal manifold-guided fusion mechanism named Early-to-late Manifold Consistency Calibration, which leverages the relatively stable global manifold preserved in early-fused encoded features to modulate robust late-stage fusion of adaptively encoded local features. Specifically, the early-stage global features serve as a structural anchor for assessing the manifold consistency of features of each adaptively encoded local view. The resulting consistency scores are then used to adaptively reweight late-stage global fusion, attenuating structurally unreliable views while reinforcing those aligned with the common manifold. In this manner, latent manifold consistency enables early fusion to calibrate late-stage fusion, thereby establishing a principled connection between adaptive view-specific encoding and cross-view distribution alignment. The full framework, named Manifold Consistency Guided Adaptive Sparse Autoencoder for Multiview Clustering (MASA), is validated on multiple datasets and demonstrates superior effectiveness and robustness across diverse experimental settings. On ALOI-100, MASA further enhances clustering stability, reducing the fluctuation standard deviation over the final rounds from 3.02% to 1.28%.

title: Bridging the Training Gap with Hyperion: A Training-Free Style Transfer Method on Diffusion Transformers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
abstract: Training-free style transfer on Multimodal Diffusion Transformers (MM-DiT) remains challenging due to the persistent gap between trained adapters and injection-based training-free methods. Existing training-free methods typically perform forward feature injection, and thus struggle to reproduce the rich painterly textures achieved by trained adapters, often leading to only faint hue shifts. In this paper, we trace this limitation to the absence of backpropagation-induced spatial coupling and propose Hyperion, a fully training-free style-transfer pipeline for MM-DiT. At the optimization level, the pipeline introduces Adam-in-loop, which iteratively optimizes the diffusion latent at each denoising step with a frozen MM-DiT. This process recovers the gradient-driven coupling effect produced through the self-attention value path, where neighboring tokens receive highly similar updates and form coherent brushstroke textures. At the distribution level, the pipeline introduces Sinkhorn Latent Transport (SLT), a single closed-form optimal-transport step that pre-aligns latent color distributions before Adam optimization, improving the operational efficiency of Adam-in-loop. To further enhance stylization quality, we develop a frequency-domain Sinkhorn loss to sharpen painterly textures and a layout-residual-suppression step to reduce layout interference. The pipeline can also be extended to image-to-image stylization. Extensive experiments on a 39-style × 6-prompt benchmark (234 pairs) demonstrate that Hyperion achieves CSD $= 0.640$ and CLIP-T $= 0.296$, improving CSD by +5.2% over Adam-8 at $2.5\times$ lower forward-pass cost and by +16.6% over Adam-only under an equal compute budget. Notably, Hyperion outperforms four pre-trained style adapters on 19 of 21 diverse style families, achieving a mean CSD of 0.657 versus 0.506 for the strongest baseline.

title: Expediting Pre-training for Vision Transformers Through Hierarchical Data Sparsity Optimization
abstract: Pre-training cost is a crucial problem in the era of the emerging large models. This is mainly caused by high model computation complexity and the million-scale training datasets, which require extensive time to train from scratch. The substantial training cost associated with recent models poses a significant barrier for individuals and institutions with limited resources. This not only impedes their ability to reach or exceed cutting-edge advancements but also restricts the practical deployment and application of these models on resource-limited devices. Most compression algorithms focus only on efficient fine-tuning or inference from the pre-trained dense models, while time-consuming pre-training is still unavoidable. In contrast, this paper points out that training data is redundant, which is the fundamental reason for the tedious training. To address the issue, this paper aims to introduce sparsity into data and proposes an end-to-end approach for pre-training acceleration by exploiting data redundancy from three sparse perspectives, dubbed Tri-Level ViT++ . Specifically, we leverage a hierarchical reduction scheme by exploring the data sparsity under three levels: the number of training samples in the dataset, the number of patches (tokens) in each sample, and the number of connections between tokens that lie in attention weights. With extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our proposed technique can noticeably accelerate both pre-training and inference for various ViT architectures while maintaining accuracy. Remarkably, under certain ratios, we are able to improve the ViT accuracy rather than compromising it. For example, we can achieve 22.3% speedup with 73.0% (+0.8) Top-1 accuracy on Deit-T, and 22.5% speedup with 80.1% (+0.3) Top-1 accuracy on Deit-S. This proves the existence of data redundancy in ViT.

title: Spatial-Frequency-Aware Implicit Neural Representation of Multidimensional Signals via MLP-KAN Fusion
abstract: Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) have emerged as a compelling paradigm for modeling multidimensional signals by mapping continuous coordinates to signal values. However, Multi-Layer Perceptrons (MLP)-based INRs inherently suffer from spectral bias, which favors low-frequency components and suppresses the reconstruction of essential high-frequency details. While existing techniques, such as Fourier feature mappings, mitigate this issue, they often rely on sensitive manual tuning and are prone to spectral artifacts. In this paper, we propose a spatial-frequency-aware INR framework that combines an MLP branch with a Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) branch for complementary frequency-oriented modeling. The MLP branch provides a low-frequency-oriented representation of smooth structures, whereas the KAN branch complements localized variations and fine details. To coordinate the two branches, we integrate the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) and inverse discrete wavelet transform (IDWT) into the output fusion stage. The outputs of the two branches are decomposed into wavelet coefficients, and the corresponding coefficients are additively fused before inverse wavelet reconstruction. A wavelet-domain band-separation regularization further penalizes high-frequency responses in the MLP branch and low-frequency responses in the KAN branch, thereby encouraging complementary frequency-oriented behavior. Experiments on 1D signals, 2D images, 3D volumes and signed distance functions, videos, and 4D light-fields demonstrate the applicability of the proposed representation across the evaluated signal modalities. Results demonstrate improved reconstruction fidelity across the evaluated signal modalities.

title: Progressive Style Transfer for Exemplar-based Open-world Sketch Colorization
abstract: Sketch colorization in open-world scenarios presents unique challenges due to diverse, unpaired datasets and the variety in user-generated sketch styles. Traditional exemplar-based methods, which typically rely on dense feature matching and style normalization, struggle to generalize effectively in these conditions, as they require structured paired data and exhibit limited flexibility. We introduce Progressive Style Transfer (PROST), a completely unsupervised framework that addresses these limitations by progressively injecting style features into sketches without rigid content-style alignment. PROST comprises two key modules: Progressive Style Injection (PSI), which transfers style features adaptively across scales, and Progressive Style Enhancement (PSE), which refines style coherence through multi-layer style-adaptive attention. Together, these modules enable flexible style transfer that preserves content fidelity while achieving high stylistic coherence. Our approach also integrates a Dual Cycle-Consistency (DCC) framework to ensure both style and content consistency in generated outputs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that PROST effectively generalizes to unseen styles, achieving robust performance across varied datasets and setting a new benchmark for open-world sketch colorization. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Vincotto/ProST.

title: Preserving Structural Irreplaceability in Token Pruning through Local Representation Complexity
abstract: The effectiveness of vision token pruning critically depends on the criterion used to define token redundancy. Existing approaches, which primarily rely on global saliency scores or similarity heuristics, often fail to account for a token's essential contribution to the model's internal representations. This oversight results in retaining visually prominent but redundant tokens or merging semantically distinct features, severely degrading performance under tight compression budgets. To address this, we propose a novel token pruning strategy aligned with representation complexity. We first introduce Local Representation Complexity (LRC), a token-level measure that estimates the intrinsic dimension of each token's embedding. Tokens exhibiting high LRC are considered locally unpredictable and are therefore prioritized for preservation. To ensure selection diversity and mitigate over-concentration in the selected set, we frame the pruning process as a budget allocation problem and introduce a Greedy Selection algorithm with Penalized Diversity to actively suppress redundancy. We evaluate the proposed method across five vision-language model backbones from three model families, including LLaVA-1.5/LLaVA-NeXT, Qwen2.5-VL/Qwen3-VL, and InternVL3, covering a wide range of capacities and tasks. The results demonstrate competitive performance across different backbones, with particularly notable gains at aggressive compression ratios.

Adaptive Distance Detection and Adaptive Instance Segmentation
abstract: This paper is about object detection model and semantic segmentation model in an FPS game Counter Strike: Condition Zero to detect enemies. Semantic segmentation is pixel-wise detection algorithm. We customized the architecture for semantic segmentation. We used YOLOv5s to train object detection model. After training, the inference time of semantic segmentation was compared to object detection. It was observed that object detection was slightly faster and semantic segmentation is slower but better at detecting the exact shape of the object. However, we found out that this slight difference of inference can grow exponentially if the both models get more complex. To solve this, we propose a novel approach called Adaptive distance detection which combines both algorithms. We will also introduce Adaptive instance segmentation to combine semantic segmentation and panoptic segmentation.

title: A Remote-Sensing Framework for Interpreting CME Transit Effects
abstract: We develop a remote-sensing framework to diagnose coronal mass ejection (CME) transit effects by comparing observed density evolution with an idealized self-similar reference shell and snowplow-based compression benchmarks. We apply the method to the 27 January 2012 CME using STEREO/SECCHI COR2-A and COR2-B and SOHO/LASCO C3. Electron-density profiles are extracted along the CME front in position-angle sectors and compared with synthetic profiles from a forward-modeled GCS shell. Sector-wise power-law fits quantify the radial density falloff and reveal substantial azimuthal variability. In COR2-A, several western sectors flatten relative to the synthetic shell and approach the snowplow-like compression regime, while other sectors show steeper-than-synthetic declines. COR2-B and LASCO C3 provide complementary viewpoints and also show sector-dependent departures, although the detailed pattern changes with viewing geometry. Conservative excess-density criteria identify clear pile-up only in localized COR2-A sectors, indicating that compression is spatially structured rather than uniform across the front. Comparison with snowplow benchmarks also depends strongly on the assumed upstream solar-wind conditions. These results show that CME-front density evolution is better described as a mixed system containing compression-dominated regions together with localized steepening that may reflect depletion, redistribution of material, or erosion-like evolution. The framework provides a practical way to separate competing processes that modify CME structure during heliospheric transit.

title: FoveaDet: Software-Hardware Co-Design of Foveated CNN-Transformer for Object Detection
abstract: Deploying real-time object detection on power-constrained edge platforms is challenging as processing full-resolution frames is often computationally redundant. Inspired by biological foveation which assigns variable resolution based on visual saliency, we propose a novel software-hardware co-design framework called FoveaDet. On the software side, FoveaDet dynamically identifies salient regions to predict fixation points, followed by aggressive patch pruning in Vision Transformers (ViT) to discard irrelevant background data. To mitigate slowdowns from sequential patch generation, we implement optimized interpolation and patch selection algorithms. Evaluated on standard GPUs, this foveated approach reduces floating-point operations by 65.4% to 92.2% and accelerates inference by 4.76x, while suffering a negligible mAP drop compared to dense baselines. To eliminate hardware bottlenecks, we complement the algorithm with a custom RISC-V core featuring specialized instructions to accelerate the foveated processing pipeline. FoveaDet provides a scalable, efficient architecture capable of unlocking advanced vision processing on severely constrained mobile platforms.

title: RipBench: A Unified Benchmark for Multi-Level Rip Current Detection, Classification and Segmentation
abstract: Rip currents are a serious and often under-addressed threat to beach safety and the leading cause of coastal drownings worldwide. They are difficult to detect due to their amorphous structure, similarity to the background, and large variability in viewpoints and environments. Despite their dangers and growing interest in automated detection, existing research remains fragmented across datasets, metrics, models, and approaches, leading to an incomplete understanding of model performance. We introduce RipBench, a unified benchmark that enables controlled evaluation of rip current detection spanning multiple tasks, including classification, axis-aligned and oriented object detection, and instance, semantic, and panoptic segmentation, on the same data with standardized splits. This allows direct comparison of model performance on all levels of visual abstraction. Across $304$ videos ($303{,}491$ frames, $51{,}011$ of them annotated for all six tasks) collected from diverse coastlines, our results expose a clear performance gap between coarse recognition and precise spatial understanding: frame-level classification reaches $F_2 = 0.93$, while the best detector and the best instance segmenter reach $0.72$ and $0.66$, with model rankings that change from task to task. Video-level confidence intervals, a blind inter-annotator study of the spatial labels, stratified analyses by viewpoint and visual signature, and video views with temporal baselines (single-seed, short-schedule reference runs) accompany the benchmark. All tasks are supported with carefully curated annotations and evaluated using standard metrics, with a focus on the $F_2$ score to emphasize recall in this safety-critical setting. RipBench, along with multiple baselines per task, is publicly available at https://RipBench.ai to support progress in real-world, multi-task vision for beach safety.

title: Reading the Table: Sim-to-Real Game State Detection for the Chef's Hat Card Game
abstract: Tabletop games offer a compelling scenario to study the interaction between artificial and human agents, combining social interaction with game state tracking and physical manipulation. To assess the game state, a robot needs to precisely detect closely related game objects, such as different card designs, requiring dedicated training data that is costly to annotate in the real world. Instead, we develop a fully automated synthetic data collection pipeline, using re-projection of known 3D coordinates to generate labels automatically and domain randomization to bridge the reality gap. This approach is used to collect a dataset of 25413 samples to finetune an object detection and a segmentation model, which are combined to assign detected cards to game-relevant zones and infer the game state. When evaluated on a real NICO humanoid robot, our pipeline achieves an F1-score of 0.906 for card-to-zone assignment, thus providing the perceptual foundation for a robot that can autonomously play Chef's Hat against human players.

title: SkillEarth: Teaching General-Purpose Agents to Act on Earth via Skill Evolution
abstract: Recently developed remote sensing (RS) agents execute real-world tasks with complex workflows through multi-step tool invocation. These agents, however, typically rely on predefined expertise or parameter updates. They thus require updating expert knowledge or retraining models whenever new tools, tasks, or execution patterns emerge, limiting their continual adaptability in dynamic Earth environments. In this work, we seek to equip general-purpose agents with RS tool-call knowledge that can be automatically extracted from demonstrated trajectories without expert intervention or parameter updates. Specifically, we propose SkillEarth, a self-evolving skill extraction method that externalizes RS tool-call knowledge as reusable, retrievable, and evolvable skill files and refines them through observation-grounded evolution. Unlike existing automatic skill extraction methods that rely on outcome-based reflection to refine skills holistically, SkillEarth grounds skill evolution in real tool-chain execution and combines dual-judge feedback with a grounded observation routing graph for precise component-level refinement. The resulting skills are generalizable, reliable, and transferable: they improve overall RS tool-call performance across three frontier LLMs and four open-source LLMs, are refined through real tool execution feedback, and support cross-model reuse without retraining. Experiments on OpenEarth-Bench and Earth-Bench demonstrate that SkillEarth achieves better tool selection, argument correctness, execution-order consistency, and task completion than existing RS agents and skill extraction methods.

title: Fear of Memorizing Objects: End-to-End Zero-Shot Model-Based Object Detection
abstract: This paper presents FOMO (Fear of Memorizing Objects), an end-to-end trainable transformer-based architecture for zero-shot model-based object detection. Existing approaches typically follow a proposal-and-match pipeline: target-agnostic mask proposals are generated and then matched to template features in a set of loosely coupled stages, making them susceptible to fragmented proposals in clutter and degraded matching under occlusions. FOMO elegantly replaces this paradigm by injecting object template information early in the detection pipeline: Bidirectional attention between learnable latent tokens, multi-view CAD templates, and query image features produces object-aware image features and conditioned queries which are subsequently decoded into bounding-box and confidence predictions. We train FOMO on Clutter6D, a novel large-scale synthetic dataset with over 500k images featuring more than 10k diverse object models rendered in highly cluttered scenes with multiple instances and varying occlusion levels, which addresses the limited object diversity and lack of realistic dense clutter in existing datasets for training zero-shot multi-instance algorithms. In true zero-shot fashion, FOMO achieves 54.2 mAP on BOP-Classic-Core at 0.23 s per image, ranking second overall with 3.8 pp difference to the top method while being more than 7x faster. Throughout comprehensive ablation studies we investigate and verify architectural design choices.

title: Learning Rate Transfer and Feature Learning Across Depth for Constrained Spectral Optimizers: Complete Scion
abstract: Hyperparameter transfer across model depth is instrumental in training deep models, as it enables learning rates calibrated on shallow networks to be effectively applied to deeper architectures. The recent CompleteP framework establishes a $1/L$ residual scaling rule that demonstrates this for Adam-family optimizers. We study whether similar transfer extends to constrained optimization methods, specifically Frank-Wolfe and projected non-Euclidean normalized steepest descent, where updates are determined by linear minimization oracles. We derive scaling rules for these methods which confirm that the $1/L$ residual scaling applies, although the arguments differ from the Adam-family optimizers. Our analysis supports depth-wise transfer and width-wise transfer of the learning rate for the Scion algorithm while ensuring feature learning and avoiding the kernel-regime. In experiments on NLP transformers (nanoGPT on FineWeb), vision transformers (DeiT on ImageNet), and vision MLPs (MLP-Mixer on CIFAR-10), we observe learning rate transfer across depth and feature learning for appropriately chosen residual scaling.

title: GingivitisSeg: A Public Dataset and Comparative Benchmark for Gingivitis Segmentation in Intraoral Images
abstract: Gingivitis segmentation from intraoral photographs can support computer-assisted periodontal assessment, but pixel-level delineation remains challenging due to severe foreground-background class imbalance, low-contrast boundaries, and variations in illumination and anatomy. We introduce GingivitisSeg, a public benchmark comprising 961 intraoral images with pixel-level annotations of gingival inflammation and predefined training (672), validation (144), and test (145) partitions. Seven semantic segmentation model-backbone configurations were compared using standardized partitions, input resolution, and evaluation metrics. Controlled ablation experiments examined class-weighted cross-entropy loss, Dice loss, and auxiliary supervision. UPerNet with ResNet50 achieved the highest mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) of 76.49% and gingivitis IoU of 54.91%. However, differences from DeepLabV3+ with ResNet50 and SegFormer with MiT-B2 were not statistically significant after Holm correction. The evaluated optimization components improved performance when combined in the UPerNet-ResNet50 configuration. Further analyses showed that performance was associated with gingivitis region size and decreased under stronger image blur. The dataset, benchmark splits, and source code are available at https://github.com/zeynepozdemir/GingivitisSeg.

title: Adapting Monocular Depth Estimation in Novel Scenes through Disparity Refinement and Robot Ego-Motion
abstract: The geometric understanding of a scene is a crucial component for safe and efficient robotic operations in novel and unstructured environments. The recent emergence of foundation models for Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE) has provided an opportunity to enrich robotic perception capabilities with dense long-range depth predictions, replacing expensive onboard hardware (e.g., LiDARs and stereo cameras). However, these offline models are primarily trained on affine-invariant depth representations, and their generalization to novel scenes remains unclear. In this work we present EM-ViT, a monocular depth estimation model that learns to adapt online relative depth inputs from a foundation model prior to the metric scale with observations collected during robotic operations. Motivated by the stereo camera parameterization, our method decomposes depth prediction via dense disparity refinement to recover the scene's relative structure and an effective baseline scalar prediction to determine the missing metric scale. The learning process leverages sparse LiDAR points and, optionally, the robot's Ego-Motion (EM) to rapidly train a lightweight Vision Transformer (ViT), while an internal gradient matching loss preserves the fine-grained semantic structure of the input disparity in real-time. We demonstrate the efficacy of our method on publicly available sequences, such as KITTI, and show that our online learning pipeline can adapt to novel scenes faster and with higher accuracy than existing MDE foundation models. The code and supplementary materials will be publicly available at https://emvit-mde.github.io.

title: RSLiveBench-UAV: A Continually Evolving Vision-Language Benchmark for Aerial Spatial Intelligence
abstract: Aerial spatial intelligence (ASI) requires models to understand objects and spatial relationships across changing viewpoints and scales. Evaluating these abilities as models evolve calls for fresh physical observations, yet producing new aerial spatial questions requires repeatedly establishing entity identities, geometric references, and cross-view correspondences. We introduce \textbf{RSLiveBench-UAV}, a continually evolving vision-language benchmark driven by recurring acquisition of real UAV imagery. Its update protocol admits images captured after the preceding release and delays answer disclosure. An entity-centered production workflow uses geometry-assisted association to link repeated observations of physical vehicles, reuse human-verified attributes, and combine them with view-specific annotations and spatial references for traceable question generation. All tasks use deterministic scoring without model judges. We evaluate 30 general-purpose, remote-sensing, and embodied models on 35,491 question records from ten scenes, covering 17 tasks across 2D perception, 3D perception, cross-view perception, and reasoning. All 18 tested embodied models outperform the three selected remote-sensing comparators in Overall, although the strongest embodied model scores 43.29 versus 59.88 for GPT-6-Astra. Fine-grained vehicle recognition remains challenging, and performance varies across heights and camera pitches. Retrospective scene-group comparisons and rolling-window replay characterize score-pattern consistency under scene renewal. RSLiveBench-UAV connects fresh physical observations, entity-centered answer production, and systematic model evaluation to support continual assessment of ASI. Benchmark will release at https://rslivebench.space

title: In-orbit demonstration of object-based change detection applied to the maritime domain
abstract: This article presents the successful in-orbit validation of an object-based change detection pipeline for low latency maritime monitoring onboard the CogniSAT-6 mission. We propose and validate a lightweight, three-phase operational sequence: optimized ground-based dual-acquisition scheduling, real-time onboard AI-based vessel segmentation, and multi-temporal matching. Upon acquiring consecutive images over a targeted Area of Interest (AoI), the onboard system correlates vessel detections using a hybrid matching approach that integrates the Hungarian algorithm for optimal assignment with RANSAC-driven spatial and size filters for outlier rejection. A series of in-orbit validations demonstrated robust performance across 11 diverse maritime scenarios, achieving valid recall and precision values (considering only vessel size and location) exceeding 0.8. The validation demonstrated the ability of the system to track both cooperative targets and uncooperative "dark" vessels strictly through geometric consistency. This capacity to autonomously generate and act upon real-time intelligence establishes a foundation for next-generation Insight-as-a-Service (IaaS) and tipping-and-cueing architectures.

title: Reliable deformation estimation of levee systems in low-coherence floodplain environments using a structure-constrained arc network (SCAN) for MT-InSAR
Monitoring peatland dynamics in the Baltic region using EGMS products
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
abstract: Climate change and the increasing regulatory requirements to preserve natural carbon sinks have intensified interest in the large-scale monitoring of peatland ecosystems, which are among the most effective terrestrial environments for long-term carbon storage and hydrological regulation. In this context, Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides an opportunity to investigate peatland dynamics over extensive areas that are difficult to survey systematically on the ground, through repeated and cost-effective observations. This study tests the transferability of an open-source and reproducible methodology for the identification and monitoring of Peat-like Behaviour Areas (PBAs), based on Advanced Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (A-DInSAR) time series provided by the European Ground Motion Service (EGMS), under the demanding observational conditions of the Boreal region, where snow cover, freeze–thaw processes and coherence loss produce sparse and discontinuous displacement series. The workflow combines Principal Component Analysis (PCA), K-means clustering and Density-Based Spatial Clustering (DBSCAN) to identify coherent areas characterised by peat-like displacement patterns and to distinguish sectors affected by subsidence from those exhibiting uplift behaviour. Applied across the Baltic countries within the Boreal biogeographical region, the methodology identified 576 PBAs (424 in Estonia, 125 in Latvia and 27 in Lithuania). A comparison with the CORINE Land Cover 2018 (CLC) inventory showed that approximately 43% of the identified PBAs occurred outside existing peatland inventories, highlighting the potential of the approach to identify areas exhibiting peat-like displacement patterns. Validation based on Sentinel-2 Total Productivity and Sentinel-3 OLCI Terrestrial Chlorophyll Index products revealed a strong spatial correspondence between the detected PBAs and areas characterised by reduced vegetation productivity and chlorophyll content. By distinguishing peatland sectors that are subsiding from those that are stable or rising, the approach provides a spatially continuous indicator of ecohydrological condition that complements static inventories, enabling degradation to be located within individual peatland systems and supporting the targeting and subsequent assessment of restoration interventions across different biogeographical regions.

title: Neighborhood-aware retrieval of a spatial floe fragmentation index for Arctic sea ice using Sentinel-1 SAR and AMSR2
abstract: Arctic sea ice fragmentation involves changes in floe area composition, spatial separation, and geometric complexity, which affect lateral melt rates and ice–ocean heat fluxes. Existing metrics primarily characterize floe size distributions or area fractions, limiting their capacity to resolve variations in the spatial arrangement of floes. We propose a spatial floe fragmentation index (SFFI) that jointly quantifies floe area composition, spatial separation, and geometric complexity. Using 416 Sentinel-1 SAR scenes spanning diverse Arctic regions and ice conditions, we extract floe contours to generate 52,074 SFFI reference labels. For samples with comparable floe area composition, higher SFFI values correspond to greater inter-floe spacing and lower circularity, demonstrating that the index captures spatial and geometric differences not represented by area composition alone. To enable daily Arctic monitoring, we develop a neighborhood-aware retrieval framework integrating AMSR2 radiometry, sea ice concentration (SIC), and neighborhood statistics, and evaluate its performance using random forest, XGBoost, and multilayer perceptron models. Under the 2016–2024 SAR-scene split, XGBoost with the complete feature set achieves the best performance, with an R2 of 0.6877, an RMSE of 0.3454, and an MAE of 0.2536. Neighborhood-aware features provide relative R2 gains of 4.6% to 10.0% over the SIC-inclusive baselines. The selected model maintained robust predictive performance on the independent 2025 dataset, supporting its temporal transferability. Using the best-performing model, we generate a daily Arctic SFFI product on a 12.5 km grid for 2016–2025. Results show that SFFI captures a pronounced seasonal cycle, with high-SFFI areas expanding during the melt season and contracting during refreezing, while revealing regional differences among Arctic marginal seas.

title: Multi-temporal analysis of reflectance and vegetation index consistency between Sentinel-2 and UAS imagery over a managed broadleaved forest: implications for monitoring
abstract: The comparability between satellite-based and uncrewed aerial system (UAS) imagery is critical for multiscale forest monitoring. It enables the integration of fine-resolution observations into a broader satellite-derived spatial and temporal context. Understanding this comparability supports the strategic use of centimeter-resolution UAS data to address fine-scale ecological questions, to serve as gap-filling observations within satellite-based time series during periods of absent data retrievals, and to link fine-scale canopy structural variation to landscape-level vegetation dynamics observed from space. This study investigated the spectral and vegetation index level consistency between Sentinel-2 and UAS multispectral measurements acquired over a 300 ha managed broadleaved forest in Central Europe. UAS data were collected using a fixed-wing platform equipped with a MicaSense Altum multispectral sensor and temporally matched to Sentinel-2 overpasses over a 6-month period at approximately two-week intervals. Cross-platform agreement was quantified using distribution-based similarity metrics, spatial aggregation of UAS data to Sentinel-2 spatial resolution, intrinsic correlation analysis, and single-date regression modeling. At their native spatial resolutions, UAS observations exhibited systematically higher radiometric variability and stronger distributional asymmetry than Sentinel-2 data, particularly in the red-edge band, consistent with increased sensitivity to fine-scale illumination differences and canopy structural heterogeneity, and partly reflecting radiometric differences between individual UAS flights. Spatial aggregation of UAS data reduced this variability but did not fully remove wavelength-dependent discrepancies, with the highest levels of agreement consistently observed in the green, red, and near-infrared bands. Among the vegetation indices, normalized difference metrics, particularly the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and the Green Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (GNDVI), showed the strongest and most temporally stable cross-platform consistency across both multitemporal distributions and individual acquisition dates. In contrast, simple ratio-based indices and indices incorporating red-edge wavelengths exhibited systematic distributional shifts and reduced temporal robustness. These distributional shifts are consistent with persistent sensor-level spectral response differences rather than index-specific artifacts.
